By leveraging correlations between frequency-shifted versions of the received signal, the FRESH filter provides optimal linear filtering for the cyclostationary processes. We first analyze the second-order statistics of OFDM signals with known structure and characterize their cyclostationary properties. Based on this analysis, we derive a compact closed-form matrix expression for the optimal FRESH filter coefficients under the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. The proposed framework enables offline computation of the filter coefficients when the signal structure is known and interference parameters are estimated, thereby reducing real-time implementation complexity. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in suppressing interference and improving detection performance compared to conventional approaches.

papers.title: Rasoi: Visual Diffs for Evaluating Structural Changes Made by Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents let developers modify software rapidly through natural language. However, as agents take on larger changes, developers can lose track of how the codebase is evolving. These edits may look correct on the surface while restructuring the system in unexpected ways: duplicating logic, changing modules outside the requested scope, removing functionality developers meant to keep, or introducing architectural drift. We investigate how visual diffs can help developers understand and evaluate the structural changes that coding agents make. We present Rasoi, a design probe that maps how a codebase's architecture evolves after each agent-made edit, letting developers inspect which architectural elements and relationships were added, modified, or removed across multiple levels of abstraction. We deployed Rasoi in a week-long study with 12 developers working on their own codebases across varied technical domains. We found that visual diffs helped developers see whether changes stayed within scope, notice unexpected restructuring, and understand how modified parts related to the system as a whole. Our findings suggest that the value of oversight tools for coding agents lies less in making developers trust the agent and more in helping developers feel confident in their own evaluation of agent-made changes. We discuss implications for visual tools that support code comprehension and human oversight in AI-assisted software development.

papers.title: Nondifferentiability on Irrational Invariant Graphs of Smooth Area-Preserving Twist Maps
papers.abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number and every $1\le r<\infty$, we construct an exact area-preserving $C^r$ twist map preserving a Lipschitz graph. The set of nondifferentiability points has Hausdorff dimension $d=2/(r+1)$ and zero $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. At the same rotation number, we construct a $C^\infty$ twist map whose invariant graph is nondifferentiable on exactly one two-sided orbit. The dynamics on these graphs has wandering intervals.

papers.title: Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
papers.abstract: Swap coboundary expansion, introduced independently by Bafna--Minzer and Dikstein--Dinur, is a local-to-global property that underlies agreement tests in the low-acceptance regime and recent constructions of succinct PCPs. Previous works obtained bounds of $\exp(-O(\sqrt{r}))$ for the $r$-swap coboundary expansion of Chapman--Lubotzky complexes. We establish the first inverse-polynomial bounds for bounded-degree complexes: suitable skeleta of Kac--Moody--Steinberg (KMS) complexes have $r$-swap coboundary expansion at least $r^{-O(1)}$. Our theorem supplies a key ingredient in forthcoming work of Ben Yaacov--Dikstein--Liu, which obtains local tests for sparse algebraic codes with guarantees even at arbitrarily small acceptance probability. These tests use $\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and guarantee that any word accepted with probability at least $\varepsilon$ agrees with a codeword on an $\varepsilon^{O(1)}$ fraction of coordinates. Separately, substituting our bound into the existing analysis of Bafna--Minzer--Vyas--Yun improves the soundness dependence of their two-query PCP construction, giving perfect completeness, soundness $\varepsilon$, and proof length $n(\log n)^{\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))}$. Our proof exploits the product structure of the groups arising in KMS complexes. The main new ingredient is a decomposition lemma for Dehn functions, which separates the analysis of group relations into independent problems on much smaller factors, with only polynomial overhead.

papers.title: Theory of interferometric background suppression for highly sensitive electro-optic sampling
papers.abstract: In electro-optic (EO) sampling, increasing the probe power enhances the EO signal, but the usable power can be limited by photodetector saturation caused by the much larger probe background independent of the applied electric field. Here, we propose a method for suppressing this background through destructive interference between an EO-modulated probe and an unmodulated reference beam. Using a Jones-matrix model, we compare five detection configurations and identify balanced detection as suitable for maintaining a linear weak-field response under strong background suppression. This suppression allows higher input optical power to be used without saturating the photodiodes, thereby enhancing the EO signal. Under a per-photodiode saturation constraint, the optimized signal enhancement scales approximately as the square root of the total input power. For a total input power of 5 W and a saturation limit of 5 mW per photodiode, the optimized configuration yields an approximately 12-fold signal enhancement over conventional balanced detection.

papers.title: Hibikino-Musashi@Home 2026 Team Description Paper
papers.abstract: This paper presents an overview of the integrated technologies developed for the Open Platform League at RoboCup@Home 2026 in Incheon. A vision system integrated with learning-based, training-free models enables robust object recognition for both known and unknown objects. We introduce a RoomPlan-based method that semi-automatically registers furniture geometry and labels to generate semantic maps. Additionally, a large language model-based planner interprets the instructions recognized by Whisper and generates primitive skill sequences for execution. A reservoir-computing framework serves as a lightweight temporal-processing model for action recognition. Its field-programmable gate array-based implementation enables low-power, real-time operation. This is key to removing operational time constraints for service robots. Open-source releases, including task environments, dataset tools, and navigation frameworks, enhance reproducibility, reuse, and continuous progress within the RoboCup@Home community.

papers.title: High Energy Asymptotics of Quark-Gluon Correlations
papers.abstract: The internal structure of the proton is encoded not only in single parton densities, but also in the quantum interference between distinct partonic configurations. We study the high energy behavior of this interference by focusing on flavor-nonsinglet quark-gluon correlations relevant to transverse spin phenomena. By establishing recursive factorization at double logarithmic accuracy in the presence of a coherent gluon insertion, we derive infrared evolution equations for the Qiu-Sterman function and its chiral odd Boer-Mulders counterpart. We find that these twist-3 functions share the leading small $x$ intercepts of their respective twist-2 counterparts, but acquire an additional $1/\ln(1/x)$ suppression due to the color structure of the coherent gluon insertion. These results may guide small $x$ extrapolations of quark-gluon correlations at the Electron Ion Collider.

papers.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares (MOLS) at 33 Orders
papers.abstract: A Latin square of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array over symbols $\{0,1,\ldots n-1\}$, such that the same symbol does not appear twice in any row or any column. Two Latin squares of order $n$ are orthogonal if, when superimposed, they yield each of the $n^2$ ordered pairs of symbols exactly once. A set of two or more Latin squares are mutually orthogonal Latin squares (MOLS) if each pair of distinct squares is orthogonal. Let $N(n)$ be the maximum size of a set of MOLS of order $n$. For most $n$ which are not prime powers, there is a wide gap between known upper and lower bounds on $N(n)$. This has led to interest in constructing new larger sets of MOLS for explicit values of $n$, to incrementally improve the lower bounds on $N(n)$. This paper provides MOLS that improve the lower bound on $N(n)$ for 33 values of $n$ in the range from 22 through 494. The constructions were found by GPT-6 Astra, and use established techniques including difference matrices, quasi-difference matrices, orthogonal arrays, and projective planes. A highlight is 4 MOLS of order $n=22$; combined with pre-existing results, this establishes $N(n) \geq 4$ for all $n>10$.

papers.title: SAGE-QA: Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Closed-Context Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0
papers.abstract: Closed-context question answering (QA) requires a system to generate an answer strictly supported by a supplied passage, or to abstain when the passage lacks adequate evidence. SQuAD 2.0 is a widely used benchmark for this setting, scored by Exact Match (EM) i.e., character-level agreement with human reference spans after lexical normalization. For generative large language models (LLMs), however, an EM failure may reflect a valid paraphrase or an alternative passage-supported answer rather than a hallucination. The best prior leaderboard EM is approximately 91%, but evaluating generative models requires separating lexical divergence from factual error. We introduce SAGE-QA (Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Question Answering), a multi-tiered framework combining reference-based Semantic Equivalence Scoring (SES) and passage-based Re-Validation Scoring (RVS). On a fixed set of 10,000 SQuAD 2.0 validation examples, we compute EM and decision-matrix F1 from TP, TN, FP, and FN counts for zero-shot closed-weight frontier models and for open-weight models, untuned and fine-tuned. Zero-shot, Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro reach 85.21 and 86.66 EM, outperforming untuned Llama 3 8B (56.88), gpt-oss-20b (66.28), and Llama 3.3 70B (71.39). Parameter-efficient fine-tuning adds 21.19 to 34.06 EM points, raising these models to 90.94, 87.47, and 94.24 EM, respectively. Auditing the frontier models with SAGE-QA and an external LLM judge yields dataset-wide SES scores of 92.81 for Claude Opus 4.6 and 91.67 for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and hybrid RVS scores, which combine benchmark credit with passage-based judge assessments, of 97.96 and 98.02. Fine-tuned open-weight models perform best, with fine-tuned Llama 3.3 70B surpassing the previous best known EM.

papers.title: LoCoJAX: Host-Local Coordination for Small-Model RL on TPUs
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly targets small language models, and executing these workloads efficiently across multiple accelerators requires effective coordination. On TPUs, Pathways-based RL uses a single controller to coordinate computation across hosts. This execution model is effective for large models, but its coordination computational costs are harder to amortize when small models repeatedly invoke short computations. To characterize these computational costs, we sweep dense models from 0.6B to 405B parameters on TPU v7x under a decode-heavy workload and measure how host and network computational overhead vary with model size. At 0.6B, host orchestration occupies 36% of step time and network communication 2%, whereas for large models, estimated network computational costs dominate the non-compute time. Motivated by these findings, we present Local Coordination JAX (LoCoJAX), which implements local rollout and reward processing on each TPU host with synchronous global training. In controlled comparisons against a tuned and optimized Pathways baseline on Qwen3-0.6B across three workloads and 8-64 TPU v7x chips, its colocated mode (LoCoJAX-CO) is 1.3-3.6x faster per step; on GSM8K, it completes a step faster on 8 chips than Pathways does on 64. Finally, a Ray-managed disaggregated mode (LoCoJAX-DA) overlaps rollout and training on separate hosts, and placement experiments establish when this overlap compensates for dividing devices and transferring weights: only when rollout dominates the step and receives most of the hosts. On NuminaMath-CoT at 256 chips, giving rollout 75% of hosts cuts step time by about 15% compared with LoCoJAX-CO.

papers.title: Smoothed Analysis for Distributed MIS
papers.abstract: We study smoothed analysis of the distributed Maximal Independent Set (MIS) problem. Luby's algorithm computes an MIS in $O(\log n)$ rounds, while the recent $Ω(\log n/\log\log n)$ lower bound of Khoury and Schild (2026) shows that it is nearly optimal even in the LOCAL model. We ask whether small random perturbations can overcome this worst-case barrier. Given an arbitrary base graph $G$ on $n$ nodes, we consider the smoothed graph $\mathcal{G}_s=G\triangle G(n,p)$, where $G(n,p)$ is an independent random graph and $\triangle$ denotes symmetric difference. Thus, each possible edge is independently toggled with probability $p$. We establish nearly tight bounds on the smoothing needed for faster distributed MIS. For every base graph $G$, when $p=β\ln n/n$ for a sufficiently large constant $β$, a randomized LOCAL algorithm, given only $\mathcal{G}_s$, computes an MIS of $\mathcal{G}_s$ in $O(\sqrt{\log n})$ rounds with high probability. This is almost quadratically faster than the worst-case lower bound. Conversely, if $p\le(1/2-δ)\ln n/n$ for a fixed constant $δ>0$, there exists a base graph on which every randomized LOCAL MIS algorithm requires $Ω(\log n/\log\log n)$ rounds on the smoothed graph. Hence, the smoothing parameter required for this speedup is optimal up to a constant factor. These results show that smoothed analysis can overcome worst-case lower-bound barriers for distributed local graph problems.

papers.title: Shallow water equations on n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds: a kinetic approach
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic kinetic moment closure for shallow-water equations on smooth manifolds of arbitrary dimension equipped with prescribed, possibly time-dependent Riemannian metrics. Hamiltonian transport on the cotangent bundle and metric-dependent momentum integration yield balance laws with hydrostatic pressure, bottom topography, a skew-adjoint force, and dissipative bottom friction. An explicit compactly supported Gibbs equilibrium satisfies the required mass, momentum, and tensor second-moment conditions. We derive the quasilinear formulation and characteristic speeds, establish the continuous mechanical-energy balance with geometric work and frictional dissipation, and obtain a weak entropy inequality for vanishing-viscosity limits under stated convergence assumptions. On the rotating sphere with a fixed round metric, the skew-adjoint force represents Coriolis effects. We construct a kinetic finite-volume scheme combining local fluxes, hydrostatic reconstruction, and geometric source terms. A second-order time integrator uses independently restricted steps at its two Euler stages. The scheme conserves discrete water volume, preserves nonnegative depth under a sufficient CFL condition, and is well balanced for lakes at rest, including wet/dry interfaces. Six-hour simulations of a localized surface disturbance over Earth topography with Manning bottom friction maintain positive depths and conserve water volume to near machine precision. Comparison with a spherical central-upwind method shows similar surface-wave propagation and gauge time series, with remaining differences in late-time local extrema.

papers.title: StateAlign: Internalizing State-Aware Decision-Making for Reliable Multi-Turn Tool Agents via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning has improved the tool-use capabilities of large language models. However, better task performance can coincide with increased tool hallucination. Reliable tool use requires decisions to follow the current task state: available information, tool capabilities, and task progress. Our analysis shows that agents sometimes execute when they should ask for information, retrieve it, or decline an infeasible request, even when reasoning identifies missing information. We introduce StateAlign, combining task-state construction with state-contrastive reinforcement learning. The data cover five task conditions and pair states with different action requirements. Outcome rewards guide task completion; token-level contrasts compare the same generated reasoning and actions under paired states to train outputs that fit the current state. Experiments across five base models from three families show improvements on BFCL v4 multi-turn, ToolSandbox, and When2Call. Ablations show that state construction improves performance and reliability under different reward designs. The complete method further reduces tool hallucination across three Qwen3 sizes. On Qwen3-8B, StateAlign improves BFCL v4 multi-turn accuracy from 45.5% to 55.2% and reduces no-tool hallucination on SimpleToolHalluBench from 62.2% under outcome-only training to 56.1%. Behavioral analyses show more consistent decisions, more complete multi-call execution, and stronger recovery after tool errors.

papers.title: Physics-Aware Transformer-Based Beamforming Optimization for Near-Field E-MIMO ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a physics-aware Transformer-based beamforming optimization (PATBO) framework for near-field extreme massive multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (E-MIMO-ISAC) systems. PATBO combines regularized zero-forcing (RZF) communication directions and spherical-wave near-field sensing directions with learned stream-power allocation. A token-preserving Transformer maintains the correspondence between individual users/targets and their allocated powers, while a Cramér--Rao bound (CRB)-sensitivity-aware objective emphasizes power-allocation errors with greater localization impact. Physical feasibility is explicitly verified after inference, with infeasible predictions handled through physics-constrained power repair and optimizer fallback. For a $32\times32$ E-MIMO array with $1024$ antennas, the proposed structured representation reduces the learned output from $12{,}288$ real-valued coefficients of an unstructured complex beamformer to six stream-power variables. Direct PATBO achieves $100.98\%$ reference-rate retention and $19.54\%$ joint feasibility, which increases to $87.79\%$ after repair. The complete hybrid framework achieves $99.89\%$ reference-rate retention and $100\%$ constraint satisfaction on the retained test set, while requiring optimizer fallback for only $12.21\%$ of the scenarios. Direct PATBO inference requires $1.11$~ms per sample, corresponding to approximately $858\times$ and $779\times$ lower runtime than the evaluated cold-start and PATBO-warm-start sequential quadratic programming (SQP) implementations, respectively.

papers.title: Overcoming Spurious Correlations in Conditional Diffusion Models via Doubly Robust Target Correction
papers.abstract: While conditional diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in generation tasks, they memorize spurious correlations within training data. This causes them to deviate from ideal target distributions. Minimizing a covariate shift-adjusted target risk can address this issue. However, retraining models from scratch for different distributions is computationally prohibitive. To overcome this limitation, we propose DR-Diff, a framework that efficiently fine-tunes pre-trained conditional diffusion models. Specifically, DR-Diff leverages a functional gradient approach to derive a pseudo-target. This pseudo-target captures the residual between the base model's noise prediction and the ground-truth noise under the target distribution. Training the model to fit this pseudo-target enables efficient target adaptation. Theoretically, we prove that DR-Diff guarantees target risk reduction at the population level. It also achieves a pseudo-doubly robust property, providing resilience against density ratio estimation errors and base model misspecifications. Empirically, DR-Diff matches the noise prediction accuracy of models trained from scratch on synthetic datasets. Furthermore, it mitigates inter-group disparities in downstream classification tasks.

papers.title: DEDCA: Test-Time Adaptation for Generalized AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.abstract: AI-generated image detectors face significant challenges when deployed in real-world environments, particularly when test samples are produced by unseen generators that deviate from the source training distribution. Existing detectors often rely on a single type of evidence, such as semantic representations or low-level generation traces, making them vulnerable when the corresponding cue becomes unreliable. Moreover, adapting detectors to newly emerging generators usually requires target labels or retraining, which is costly and impractical. To address these challenges, we propose Dual-Evidence Disagreement-Constrained Adaptation (DEDCA), a test-time adaptation framework for generalized AI-generated image detection. DEDCA constructs a dual-evidence detector by combining CLIP-based semantic evidence with trace evidence extracted from shuffled entropy and residual statistics, and introduces a reliability-aware gate to perform sample-specific adaptive fusion. Our key idea is to exploit the disagreement between the two evidence streams as an unlabeled adaptation signal, enabling the detector to adjust to target-domain shifts without relying on target labels or blindly trusting a single prediction stream. Experiments show that DEDCA achieves superior performance on the GenImage benchmark by outperforming state-of-the-art AI-generated image detectors and test-time adaptation methods with 92.0\% average accuracy.

papers.title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram
papers.abstract: Knowledge of phase stability is the first requirement for materials design, and predicting the conditions under which new materials can be synthesized has become a key capability of self-driving laboratories (SDLs). For inorganic materials, notably alloys, these predictions come from thermodynamic databases built with the CALPHAD method. Building a database, however, requires expert judgment at many steps, and because these decisions are rarely recorded, others can use a database but cannot regenerate or update it. Machines can already collect the data, build a first model with machine-learned interatomic potentials and refine it against experiments. The assessment itself, the sequence of judgments that turns these parts into a reliable database, is still carried out by human experts. We argue that it can be automated reproducibly only if the expert knowledge behind an assessment is encoded in formal protocols, so that an assessment delivers a record of its construction and not only its parameters. We introduce ORCHID-SAGE, a standard that organizes this record into reproducible and automatable protocols. In this first attempt, applied to Cr-Ni, the database was regenerated from its record by a script on a second machine, by an AI agent working only through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and by a refit from public sources only, with the same predictions. Recorded in this way, a database need no longer be fixed at publication but can be updated by AI agents as SDLs and other sources provide new evidence, while the judgment remains with people and on the record.

papers.title: Generalized Kosmann derivative and symmetry operators on Dirac structures
papers.abstract: We develop a spinorial symmetry framework for metric Dirac structures in $H$-twisted exact Courant algebroids. A generalized metric equips a Dirac structure with an intrinsic Riemannian Lie-algebroid geometry and identifies it isometrically with the positive subbundle of the generalized tangent bundle. For sections preserving the generalized metric, we prove an exact intertwining between the positive-spinor Kosmann--Dorfman action and the intrinsic Kosmann derivative. The comparison is independent of the auxiliary compatible generalized connection. Within the intrinsic geometry we derive Killing--Yano (KY) and conformal Killing--Yano (CKY) integrability identities, construct Killing-spinor-preserving operators from odd special KY and even special closed CKY forms, and obtain these forms from Hermitian bilinears of Killing spinors with imaginary Killing number. We illustrate the framework on a global Dirac structure over $S^2\times S^1$ with nontrivial $H$-flux class and rank-two anchor. Its spin connection and symmetry operators are explicit, and its Killing-spinor space is a transverse family $C^\infty(S^1,\mathbb C^2)$. Finally, intrinsic Killing sections act on Killing spinors by a Lie algebra representation. For a graph Dirac structure over $S^3$, the odd Jacobi identity of the Hermitian-current bracket fails by a phase, and adjoining a single even phase generator yields a Lie superalgebra. These results connect generalized isometries, hidden spinorial symmetries, and flux-sensitive Lie-algebroid geometry.

papers.title: Selective Generative Restoration for Video Deraining via Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion
papers.abstract: Video deraining is challenging due to rain streaks, occlusions, and atmospheric effects. Existing methods mainly follow a deterministic restoration paradigm, assuming that clean scenes can be uniquely recovered from rainy observations. However, rain degradation is spatially heterogeneous. Reliable regions require faithful reconstruction, whereas severely occluded regions contain ambiguous content that require stronger prior-driven inference. Therefore, conventional deterministic restoration often produces over-smoothed results, while global generative restoration may introduce unnecessary hallucinations. We introduce a Selective Generative Restoration paradigm for video deraining, where generative priors are adaptively activated according to restoration uncertainty. Based on this principle, we propose Selective Generative Video Deraining (SGVD), an uncertainty-aware diffusion framework that enables adaptive fidelity preservation and generative recovery. Specifically, SGVD exploits stochastic diversity between dual one-step diffusion predictions to estimate region-level restoration uncertainty, which determines where observation fidelity should be preserved and where generative inference should be activated. Furthermore, an anchor-guided trajectory consistency mechanism is proposed to regularize stochastic diffusion evolution across frames, reducing temporal generation drift and improving video coherence. To achieve practical efficiency, SGVD adopts one-step diffusion inference while maintaining uncertainty-aware generative capability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SGVD achieves superior restoration performance, perceptual quality, and temporal consistency compared with state-of-the-art video deraining methods.

papers.title: What Does It Cost to Force-Close a Lightning Channel? Evidence from 974,000 Channel Closes, 2018-2026
papers.abstract: Bitcoin's Lightning payment network returns the funds of a channel that cannot close cooperatively through pre-signed transactions whose fees and delays fall on its operators. That fee design is being replaced: Bitcoin Core 31.0 removed the mempool rule anchor channels relied on, and the Lightning specification adopted zero-fee commitments in May 2026. What the old design costs has never been measured across fee regimes. We trace every public channel close and every force close on-chain from January 2018 to October 2026, 973,581 closes, and follow each output to its spend. A separate chain index confirms all 698,476 public closes we could compare. Fee spikes did not bring a wave of force closes. Force closes in a spike week and the next were 0.97 times the four weeks before, against 1.02 after ordinary weeks of the same years. A force close costs 2-6 times a cooperative close in fees and locks the closer's balance for days, which outweighs the fees only in low-fee years. When fees are high, pending payments are exposed: in 2023, 18.2% of HTLC timeouts confirmed more than 40 blocks after expiry. Yet since 2021, forwarding nodes lost only 38 payments, each with the preimage already on-chain. Anchor outputs cut late timeouts in fee spikes (20.6% against 30.5%), yet owners rarely bump commitments with them, and miners take most of what third parties sweep. Zero-fee commitments would save only 12% of the anchor mechanism's block space; they should be judged by how promptly payments resolve when fees spike.

papers.title: Alloy: A Multi-Material Physics Engine for Robot Learning
papers.abstract: Robots handle much more than rigid objects: towels, cables, water, sand. The simulators used to train robots at scale are strongest on rigid bodies, and adding another material usually means a second engine and hand-written glue between the two. We present Alloy, an open-source physics engine for robot learning in which rigid robots, cloth, cables, liquids, granular material and soft bodies share one scene. Each object is described once; Alloy assigns it to a solver suited to its material, couples the solvers inside every control step, and runs the scene in many parallel worlds on one GPU, or on a CPU. Every world carries a health grade, to help tell a failure of the physics from a failure of the policy. Alloy is built on Newton, MuJoCo Warp and Warp, and it is written to be driven by coding agents: its documentation ships inside the package, every error names its fix, and the engine is exposed as tools over the Model Context Protocol. In a cold test, agents that had never seen Alloy installed a pre-release from the package index and trained policies for walking, cable handling and pouring on a single GPU. We also report how throughput grows with the number of worlds, depth-camera throughput, agreement with closed-form references, and a reliability test over a thousand worlds.

papers.title: Optimal-Size Strong Connectivity Preservers under Two Edge Failures in Subcubic Time
papers.abstract: A $k$-edge-failure strong connectivity preserver of a directed graph on $N$ vertices is a spanning subgraph that has the same strongly connected components as the input after each set of at most $k$ edge deletions. The lower-bound construction of Baswana, Choudhary, and Roditty [BCR18], adapted to strong connectivity in [CC20], gives the previous best bound of $Ω(2^kN)$ necessary edges. Hoppenworth, Saranurak, and Wang [HSW25] prove an $O(k4^kN\log N)$ upper bound, leaving a logarithmic gap for fixed $k$. We close this gap by giving an explicit strongly connected graph on $N=2^d$ vertices with $N-1+(N/2)\log_2N$ edges, every one of which is necessary in a two-failure preserver. Together with the upper bound of [HSW25], this proves that the optimal size in the worst case is $Θ_k(N\log N)$ for every fixed $k\geq2$, whereas it is $Θ(N)$ for $k=1$ [GIP20]. The same graph has a one-failure preserver with at most $3(N-1)$ edges. We also give a randomized algorithm that either returns a spanning subgraph or reports failure. For every fixed $c,\varepsilon>0$, with probability at least $1-N^{-c}$ it returns a correct preserver for $k=2$ with $O(N\log N)$ edges, in $\widetilde O(N^{(ω+3)/2+\varepsilon})$ time and $\widetilde O(N^2)$ space. Here $ω$ is the matrix multiplication exponent over a fixed finite field.

papers.title: Rigidity of compact quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary and low-dimensional focal sets
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate nontrivial compact m-quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary, m > 1 and constant scalar curvature. We first prove that such a manifold is rigid whenever the set of critical points of its potential function is totally geodesic, which extends to quasi-Einstein manifolds a theorem of Li, Li, Ou, Qu, Wu and Zhou for shrinking Ricci solitons. Then, we prove that, in every dimension, this set is totally geodesic whenever it has dimension two or three, so that the manifold is rigid in this case. The proof is based on a Bochner identity for the covariant derivative of the Ricci tensor at the points of this set. In particular, every such manifold of dimension five is rigid. Finally, we obtain rigidity in arbitrary dimension under an integral Weyl pinching condition when the set of critical points has dimension four.
authors: Matheus Andrade Ribeiro de Moura Horácio

papers.title: Shared Item-Level Error Limits the Aggregation of Small Language Models in Fermi Estimation
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems of language models are often motivated by an averaging argument: if the agents' errors are unbiased and independent, the error of an aggregate of N answers falls as 1/sqrt(N). Fermi estimation, whose continuous answers are aggregated on the logarithmic scale, permits a direct test. We decompose the log10 error of each answer into the mean error of its model on the item, common to all its draws on the item, and a residual, and estimate both from 2.51M answers given before any communication by 15 open-weight models (3B-72B) on realFP, with replication under a single prompt pair on realFP, Science Olympiad Fermi questions and a guesstimation set. Given the item, teammates' errors are uncorrelated and teams behave as independent draws, but the item-level component accounts for a median 0.906 of the error variance over items. Teams of thirty therefore reduce a single agent's error by a median 1.7% (at most 5.4%), whereas draws that were also unbiased on each item would reduce it by 74-79%. All models compress their estimates toward about 10^6; this trend explains a median 17% of the item-level component, and a cross-validated linear recalibration on labelled items removes the overall bias but not that component. Three rounds of debate reduce within-team dispersion by 93% and leave the item-level component unchanged; revision without peers attains the same small gain. Mixing five models of similar accuracy reduces error by 6.6% relative to their own homogeneous teams, but no mixture improves on the most accurate model. Higher sampling temperature changes team error by about 1% at most, and contrastive activation steering not detectably; per-agent scaffold prompts (not significant after multiplicity correction) and skipping one layer in a single-model screen improve it. The results are conditional on the models, benchmarks, prompts and settings tested.

papers.title: Laser cooling of $\mathrm{Th}^{-}$: Revised bound-state structure and a more efficient cooling scheme
papers.abstract: The thorium anion ($\mathrm{Th}^{-}$) has been proposed as a candidate for laser cooling of negative ions. However, previous theoretical and experimental results exhibit significant discrepancies in both the excitation energies and lifetimes. Here we revisit the bound-state structure and transition properties of $\mathrm{Th}^{-}$ using two independent ab initio approaches. The two calculations agree well and improve agreement with measured excitation energies and lifetimes. Based on the present level structure, we reassign several observed levels and show that the previously proposed $^4F^e_{3/2}\leftrightarrow{}^2S^o_{1/2}$ cooling transition is not closed and requires two repumping lasers. We therefore propose an alternative cooling scheme based on the $^4F^e_{3/2}\leftrightarrow{}^4F^o_{3/2}$ transition, which requires only one repumping laser and has a transition rate approximately five times larger ($A\approx1.1\times10^5$ s$^{-1}$), the fastest reported bound--bound E1 transition in atomic anions to date.

papers.title: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization
papers.abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization enables memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models through forward-only evaluations, but high-dimensional random perturbations can limit optimization efficiency. Sparse perturbations reduce the search dimension, making the selection of informative coordinates critical. We propose Wanda-Importance Sparsity-MeZO (WIS-MeZO), which uses Wanda weight--activation saliency to construct task-conditioned sparse perturbation masks while keeping the pretrained model dense. We analyze support quality through gradient energy capture and relate it to gradient estimation and convergence. Across 16 benchmarks with LLaMA and Qwen models ranging from 3B to 32B parameters, WIS-MeZO achieves higher aggregate scores than MeZO and reaches comparable validation losses in fewer optimization steps. Comparisons with random and magnitude-based sparse perturbations further highlight the importance of informative support selection.

papers.title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors
papers.abstract: We evaluate LLM risk propensities across a range of contexts and task demands. We evaluate models for how risk averse or risk tolerant they are in various conditions, as well as how stable and consistent their behavior is across conditions. We present a toolkit for developing model risk profiles that can be used to predict model behavior and which can be adapted to include new evaluations of risk propensities. We also examine how these properties have changed across model generations and families. We observe that 2026 state-of-the-art models tend to be more stable, more consistent, and more risk neutral than older models. These trends appear to be related; newer models are more stable and consistent because they are more likely to use expected value maximization as a decision procedure.

papers.title: Global-in-time dynamics of the pressureless Euler/incompressible non-Newtonian equations
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a two-phase fluid system on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}^3$, consisting of the pressureless Euler equations and the incompressible non-Newtonian equations coupled through a drag force. We prove the global-in-time existence of strong solutions to this system for a certain class of stress tensors in the non-Newtonian fluid. Our proof combines a priori large-time behavior estimates for classical solutions with a bootstrapping argument on the $L^2$-Sobolev norms, which effectively handles the difficulties caused by the lack of dissipation in the density of the Euler equation.

papers.title: 3D radiative transfer of K-series lines of He-like ions with SKIRT
papers.abstract: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy with XRISM has resolved line profiles of highly ionised ions, including P Cygni profiles, in many systems containing compact objects. To interpret these line profiles, forward modelling with three-dimensional radiative transfer (3D RT) calculations including the relevant ionic processes is required. Following our previous work on the Lyman-series lines of H-like ions, we present the implementation of the K-series lines of He-like ions with Z = 2-30 in the open-source Monte Carlo RT code SKIRT, providing a numerical tool for interpreting highresolution X-ray spectra of photoionised plasmas. Building upon the framework developed for H-like ions, we incorporate the resonance scattering (RS) and radiative recombination (RR) channels. We also implement the inner-shell ionisation (II) channel of Li-like ions for the production of He-like lines. We resolve fine-structure levels and account for level populations, frequency redistribution, phase function, and linear polarisation through transition-specific Mueller matrices. The implementation reproduces the expected RT effects in He-like lines. The Fe xxv w and y lines, dominated by the RS channel, develop optically thick line-profile distortions and P Cygni profiles in an outflowing plasma, whereas the x and z lines, dominated by the RR and II channels, do not exhibit such behaviour. The line intensities from the RS and RR channels agree well with Cloudy. The II channel further enhances the z line, which is not yet included in Cloudy. The linear polarisation calculations reproduce the analytical and experimental angular dependence of resonance scattering on a line-by-line basis. This extension to He-like lines, together with our previous implementation of H-like lines, enables 3D RT modelling of the major X-ray lines, providing a tool for constraining gas kinematics around compact objects observed with XRISM.

papers.title: From Large Language Models to Efficient System One Models via Adaptive Computation
papers.abstract: Transferring LLMs into System One decision models typically replaces the language modeling head with a decision head while retaining the full backbone, making every decision pay for all layers. Yet it remains unclear how much depth such decisions require. We find that decision information is concentrated in intermediate layers, with early layers building essential features and the final six layers removable without loss, while independently trained smaller models largely mimic the full model rather than developing specialized decision capabilities. These findings suggest that efficiency requires not simply smaller backbones, but shared computation across different depths. Building on this, we propose \method{}, which jointly trains a full model with prefix sub-models that share its final layers and decision head through self-distillation. A lightweight gate reads the hidden state at each exit to determine whether additional computation is needed, allowing one model to operate at multiple layers. Across seven decision benchmarks, our approach matches or outperforms independently trained models at every depth, while achieving better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs through adaptive computation.

papers.title: Climate Temporal Temperature Prediction via an Adaptive Stacked Bidirectional Residual Mamba Network
papers.abstract: Accurate temperatures forecasting relies on traditional meteorological parameters that are essential for monitoring weather informatics and guiding forecasting efforts. This study presents Deep DualMamba, a novel deep learning framework for temporal temperature prediction, built upon an enhanced variant of the recently proposed Mamba network. Unlike conventional Transformer-based architectures, which dominate foundation models but suffer from computational inefficiencies on long sequences, Deep DualMamba leverages selective structured state space models (SSMs) to achieve both scalability and performance. We identify a core limitation of prior subquadratic-time models-namely, their inability to perform long-term and robust forecasting and introduce two key innovations. First, we propose an adaptive bidirectional Mamba as encoders to learn complex and efficient features. Second, we develop a hardware-aware, parallel recurrent algorithm to compensate for the loss of convolutional efficiency, ensuring practical viability at scale. Last, the Deep DualMamba's approximation ability and convergence is theoretical analyzed. These design choices culminate in a simplified, attention- and MLP-free neural architecture that exhibits linear complexity with sequence length and significantly improved inference throughput. To demonstrate its applicability in climate informatics, we implement a full forecasting pipeline using historical meteorological data from UK monitoring stations.

papers.title: Does Deep Knowledge Tracing Learn Semantic Relations Between Knowledge Components?
papers.abstract: Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) is a knowledge tracing (KT) model that updates a shared latent state from sequences of interactions, each pairing a knowledge component (KC) with a response. An interaction with one KC can therefore affect predictions for other KCs. We ask: Are the KC relations learned by DKT semantic? We construct text-derived semantic KC representations using nine pipelines to test whether the conclusions hold across alternative ways of constructing those representations. The first test compares DKT-derived KC relation graphs with semantic relation structures induced by pairwise cosine similarities among the KC representations. Across the evaluated datasets, embedding models, and pipelines, the two structures align only weakly and inconsistently. The second test introduces semantic information into DKT; the pretrained text-derived representations do not consistently outperform the standard DKT baseline. In the reduced-data experiments, semantic initialization yields a higher test area under the ROC curve (AUC) than the baseline at eight of nine nested sample sizes for ASSISTments 2017. KC-supervised fine-tuned BERT produces small positive AUC differences in some matched comparisons, but the study does not establish their stability across runs. These effects remain limited and inconsistent. The findings suggest that behavioral, temporal, structural, or psychometric signals may also shape DKT's learned relations. DKT-derived relations are not primarily semantic: the tested text-derived semantic structures do not strongly recover the DKT-derived relation structure.

papers.title: Galaxy Clustering Topology in Observations and Cosmological Simulations
papers.abstract: We present a genus topology analysis of the large-scale distribution of galaxies in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey Data (SDSS), comparing the observed topology with mock galaxy samples from the Horizon Run 4 (HR4) $N$-body simulation and four cosmological hydrodynamical simulations. We construct nine volume-limited samples and measure their genus curves at Gaussian smoothing scales of $4$--$12~h^{-1}{\rm Mpc}$. Overall, the modern galaxy models reproduce the observed genus statistics substantially better than the HGC, HOD, and SAM models examined by Choi et al. (2010). Among the models considered here, the HR4 Most-Bound-Halo Particle galaxy-assignment model shows somewhat better overall agreement with the SDSS topology than IllustrisTNG300 and FLAMINGO. The observed scale dependences of the genus shift parameter $Δν_f$ and void abundance parameter $A_V$ are somewhat steeper than those predicted by the simulations, but their joint discrepancy from HR4 is not statistically significant. The smaller-volume TNG100 and EAGLE realizations show significant excesses in $A_C$, at $4.5σ$ and $7.0σ$, respectively, relative to the observational uncertainties. When the expected cosmic variance of the simulations is taken into account, they do not necessarily indicate failures of the galaxy-formation prescriptions, but they caution that individual small-volume realizations may not be representative of the observed galaxy topology. Overall, modern galaxy formation models reproduce the observed topology substantially better than earlier models, while residual differences remain that can be tested more precisely with denser future surveys.

papers.title: Optimal staircase structure for bacterial adaptation in antibiotic landscapes
papers.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in antibiotic environments drives the evolution of bacterial resistance. However, how the discrete structure of these environments controls the time required for adaptation of bacteria remains unclear. We study this question using a stochastic model on a two-dimensional lattice whose axes represent physical space and phenotype space, comparing different numbers of steps while holding the overall spatial and concentration ranges fixed and scaling the migration and mutation rates by their end-to-end first-passage times. We find that increasing the number of steps accelerates the search for the next adapted state but increases the cumulative cost of repeated population saturation; this competition can produce an optimum at an intermediate number of steps. Direct Gillespie simulations reproduce the predicted dependence of the adaptation time on the number of steps, providing testable predictions for how discrete environmental structure shapes the timescale of evolutionary adaptation.

papers.title: Tracing dependency networks explains how origins shape downstream vulnerability
papers.abstract: Many systems sustain outcomes through chains of prerequisites, yet these dependencies are often partially observed. We trace backward from sampled outcomes to recover dependency structure and measure edge importance by the fraction of outcomes lost after an edge fails. Across 1,620 synthetic networks, revealing 90% of origins required tracing 7.24% of outcomes on average. We define pair thickness as the number of origin and outcome pairs connected through an edge. Under strict dependency, where every input is necessary, thickness counts each affected outcome once per upstream origin, whereas loss counts it once. Edges therefore form origin groups with distinct thickness and loss relations, also seen in software, citation and river topologies. Within a network, greater origin diversity corresponds to lower strict loss at equal complete thickness. We develop a growth model that predicts how edges populate these groups and how losses are distributed under partial observation, tested on 2,560 independent networks. Separating origin counts from downstream reach improves identification of edges causing the greatest losses among unsampled outcomes in strict synthetic tests. Substitutable inputs reduce losses and change which importance scores perform best. Edge importance thus measures a dependency's contribution to sustaining later outcomes, guiding the protection of critical connections.

papers.title: Designing Information in a Forest: Algorithmic Aspects
papers.abstract: The Bayesian persuasion framework models strategic information revelation by a sender to one or more receivers. We study an intricate version of the multi-receiver persuasion setting in which the communication hierarchy is a forest - i.e., some receivers observe more informative signals than others, and the partial ordering of the receivers according to the information they get is represented by a pre-specified directed forest. This model naturally captures interactions in hierarchical organizations, and it lies in between the two most commonly studied versions of Bayesian persuasion: private persuasion and public persuasion. Inspired by the classic model of private persuasion, we focus on a setting with a binary state of nature and binary-action heterogeneous receivers s.t. the sender's utility is a monotone function of the set of receivers taking a specific desirable action. We extend the computational tractability result for symmetric sender's utility from private persuasion to the forest hierarchy framework using methodology inspired by optimal transport theory. We further provide a polynomial-time algorithm when the sender's utility is modular. On the negative side, we show that, unlike in private persuasion, the case of a supermodular sender's utility function leads to an NP-hard optimization problem which further does not admit an FPTAS unless P=NP; this result holds even when each tree component of the forest is a chain of 3 receivers. To complement the hardness result, we provide a simple approximation algorithm with the approximation ratio depending linearly on the depth of the forest hierarchy. We further provide an analogous algorithm for the submodular utility case. Finally, beyond forest communication hierarchies, we rule out an FPTAS for the sender's optimal utility even in the symmetric utility case, unless P=NP.

papers.title: Counting circles in Kleinian circle packings
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a bounded Kleinian circle packing with symmetry group $Γ$, and let $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ denote the number of circles in $\mathcal{P}$ of radius at least $T^{-1}$. We obtain an asymptotic formula for $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ in which the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator below the continuous spectrum contribute a finite sum of main terms, with an error term having the same exponent as in the counting theorem of Lax--Phillips for $Γ$-orbits in $\mathbb H^3$.

papers.title: Information Thermodynamics in Closed Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
papers.abstract: Although information thermodynamics explains how the second law is modified due to the information acquired by Maxwell's demon, its formulation in many-body systems remains largely open. Here, we develop an information-thermodynamic framework for closed quantum many-body systems initially in microscopic thermal equilibrium (MITE), under physically motivated restrictions: local quantum measurements and finite-time controls generated by local Hamiltonians. By additionally assuming that each local feedback term depends only on nearby measurement outcomes, we rigorously prove that the extractable work coincides in the thermodynamic limit with that extractable from the corresponding canonical ensemble. We further express this extractable work in terms of quantum-information quantities, including the quantum-classical mutual information and the Holevo information for the corresponding canonical ensemble. We also show that feedback based on distant measurement outcomes can exploit long-range correlations hidden in MITE, yielding an extensive increase in extracted work relative to the canonical ensemble.

papers.title: Snoopie: A Multi-GPU Communication Profiler and Visualizer
papers.abstract: With data movement becoming one of the most expensive bottlenecks in computing, the need for profiling tools to analyze communication becomes crucial for effectively scaling multi-GPU applications. While existing profiling tools including first-party software by GPU vendors are robust and excel at capturing compute operations within a single GPU, support for monitoring GPU-GPU data transfers and calls issued by communication libraries is currently inadequate. To fill these gaps, we introduce Snoopie, an instrumentation-based multi-GPU communication profiling tool built on NVBit, capable of tracking peer-to-peer transfers and GPU-centric communication library calls. To increase programmer productivity, Snoopie can attribute data movement to the source code line and the data objects involved. It comes with multiple visualization modes at varying granularities, from a coarse view of the data movement in the system as a whole to specific instructions and addresses. Our case studies demonstrate Snoopie's effectiveness in monitoring data movement, locating performance bugs in applications, and understanding concrete data transfers abstracted beneath communication libraries. The tool is publicly available at https://github.com/ParCoreLab/snoopie.

papers.title: Statistical correlations between turbulent structures and dissipation proxies in near-Earth space: the MMS 2023-2024 unbiased magnetosheath campaign
papers.abstract: The terrestrial magnetosheath provides excellent opportunities for the experimental study of space plasma physics. Turbulence and kinetic-scale dissipation processes have been extensively studied separately. However, examining their cross-scale interplay may shed light on unsolved long-standing questions: which kinetic processes specifically dissipate the plasma turbulent fluctuations, and what drives them? In this study, we perform a statistical study of high-resolution data from the 2023-2024 unbiased campaign of the Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission to examine correlations between local small-scale accumulation of turbulent energy and peaks of dissipation proxies. The results highlight that clear regional correlations between a vast ensemble of dissipation proxies emerge on a scale of a few ion inertial lengths. Furthermore, intermittent turbulent structures dissipate energy in a hierarchical ordering

papers.title: Estimates of the Schwarz constant for monogenic functions in $\mathbb R^3$
papers.abstract: The Schwarz lemma bounds the differential at the origin of a holomorphic self-map of the unit disc fixing $0$: $|f'(0)|\le1$. For monogenic maps in $\mathbb R^3$, the optimal constant is not known. Let $\mathcal M$ be the class of monogenic functions $f$ from the unit ball of $\mathbb R^3$ to the reduced quaternions with $|f|\le1$ and $f(0)=0$, and let $C_*=\sup_{\mathcal M}|f'(0)|$, where $f'=\partial_0f$ is the hypercomplex derivative. We show that $\frac{80}{61}\le C_*\le1.35784$. Thus the classical bound $1$ fails, while $C_*$ stays below the sharp constant $\frac32$ for harmonic maps of the ball into itself. The estimates rest on a reduction, by rotation covariance and averaging about the $x_0$-axis, to a convex extremal problem in one variable for zonal harmonic functions. Lower bounds come from restricting this problem to polynomials, and upper bounds from its dual formulation in terms of vector fields on the sphere.

papers.title: When Elements Fail: Weighted Fault-Tolerant Matroid Bases
papers.abstract: Given a rank-\(r\) matroid on \(n\) elements with nonnegative costs and a partition into safe and vulnerable elements, we seek a minimum-cost set that spans after every deletion of at most \(k\) selected vulnerable elements. We resolve several open questions posed by Bentert, Fomin, Golovach, and Morelle (ESA 2025) concerning weighted costs, nonuniform failures, and explicitly specified failure scenarios. To this end, we develop two compression methods. For matroids given by an independence oracle, weighted flat-avoidance representatives yield a bounded subset of the ground set containing an optimal solution and a \(2^{\mathcal{O}((r+k)^4)}n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}\)-time algorithm. This establishes fixed-parameter tractability for weighted costs and nonuniform failures simultaneously. For explicitly represented linear matroids, polynomial certificates allow us to compress families of partial solutions while preserving successful completions under all allowed failures. This yields a deterministic algorithm using \(2^{\mathcal{O}(kr(r+k)\log(r+1))}n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}\) field operations over arbitrary fields. Over fixed finite fields, a simpler reduction uses parallel classes. For explicitly listed failure scenarios, we obtain fixed-parameter algorithms parameterized by rank and the number of scenarios. In contrast, the size-budget decision version is W[1]-hard parameterized by rank and maximum scenario size, even on uniform matroids with two-element scenarios. \keywords{Matroids \and Fault tolerance \and Fixed-parameter algorithms \and Representative families}

papers.title: Collective information backflow from a local population record: Identifiability and learning
papers.abstract: Information backflow in a composite quantum system is defined through pairs of evolving states, whereas an experiment may provide only a restricted population record. We study this mismatch for two identical qubits coupled collectively to a vacuum reservoir with an exponential correlation function. An ideal bright-state population trajectory determines the bath-parameter combinations relevant to a finite-time trace-distance backflow diagnostic of the full two-qubit channel, evaluated on a fixed time grid and state-pair bank. The unresolved detuning sign leaves this diagnostic unchanged. This relation allows sparse population records to predict the diagnostic using support-vector learning or direct physical fitting. Finite measurement statistics impose a different restriction: a two-hypothesis bound identifies reservoirs with similar short population records but substantially different backflow. For one six-time protocol with 600 total shots, every estimator using those observations has expected absolute error at least approximately 0.13 at one of two specified reservoirs. Thus a population can be sufficient within a known bath family without permitting uniformly accurate inference from a short noisy record.

papers.title: From More to Better: Causal Inference and Digital Experimentation in the Age of AI
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is quickly expanding the capacity of organizations to produce and analyze data. We argue that this expansion shifts the leverage of data scientists from performing individual analyses to assessing the credibility and importance of findings and determining when evidence generalizes across contexts. Drawing on a roundtable of academic researchers and industry practitioners, we examine three ways in which data scientists who work on causal inference and experimentation can help organizations turn more analytical capacity into better decisions: preserving and accumulating the learning value of experimentation beyond individual tests; choosing and combining experimental, observational, and synthetic evidence; and ensuring evaluation keeps pace with AI as its capabilities and uses evolve. In each area, we distinguish established practice from open questions. We conclude with implications for the training and practice of data science and for organizations.

papers.title: Visibility graphs of irregularly sampled two-dimensional fields via Voronoi tessellations
papers.abstract: Visibility graphs map a time series into a network by linking two data whenever the straight line between them is not obstructed by intermediate data. Their extension to two-dimensional fields has so far been restricted to regular lattices, where visibility is checked along a finite number of lattice directions. We propose a definition for scalar data sampled at arbitrary, irregularly scattered points of the plane. Each point is assigned its Voronoi cell, so that the data become a landscape of prisms, and two points are linked when the line of sight between them clears the cells crossed by the connecting segment. This yields horizontal ($\HVGV$) and natural ($\NVGV$) Voronoi visibility graphs that reduce exactly to the classical horizontal and natural visibility graphs when the points are collinear, contain the Gabriel graph of the point set, and can be built by an exact walk through the Delaunay triangulation. For uncorrelated heights, the horizontal graph depends only on the ranks of the data, so its statistics are independent of the marginal distribution. The probability that two points see each other is $2/[(M+1)(M+2)]$, where $M$ is the number of Voronoi cells crossed, which reduces the problem to the geometry of the tessellation. For Poisson points this gives a degree distribution with a scale-free tail $P(k)\simeq(π^3/4)\,k^{-2}$ and a mean degree that grows as $(π^3/8)\ln N$, in contrast with the finite value $\langle k\rangle=4$ of one-dimensional series. Two dimensions are therefore the marginal case in which isotropic horizontal visibility ceases to be local. Numerical simulations with up to $N=1.28\times10^5$ points support these predictions.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Parallel Policy Learning for Collapse-Reactive Retreat via Hybrid Terrain Modeling
papers.abstract: At disaster sites and on unstable slopes, robot contact can collapse uninspected terrain, requiring retreat upon support loss. Massively parallel reinforcement learning of collapse-reactive retreat requires independent state--action experiences. However, on shared rigid-body collapsible terrain, one robot's collapse alters others' contacts without direct interaction. We call this indirect interference. Duplicating terrain objects prevents this but is memory-intensive, limiting parallel sampling. Our key insight is that policy learning does not necessarily require rigid-body collapse modeling, which is feasible but computationally expensive; collapse-induced contact responses can suffice. We therefore propose a memory-efficient parallel policy-learning framework for collapse-reactive retreat via hybrid terrain modeling. Hybrid terrain modeling combines rigid-body simulation of non-collapsible terrain with virtual contact forces for collapsible regions. A State-Multiplexed Contact Model shares terrain geometry and a contact-response law while maintaining environment-specific collapse states, enabling independent experiences without terrain objects for collapsible regions. The framework trains a proprioceptive policy for both normal locomotion and collapse-reactive retreat. It supports over 100 times as many parallel environments as fine-resolution rigid-block terrain within the same GPU memory limit. This scalability and improved sample efficiency enable over 50 times faster policy convergence with comparable retreat performance. Sim-to-sim and real-robot experiments demonstrate retreat under multiple collapse conditions. A supplementary video is available at: https://youtu.be/_RrhwjzEPE0

papers.title: Total edge irregularity strength of cubic graphs
papers.abstract: We show that every finite simple cubic graph on $n$ vertices has total edge irregularity strength $n/2+1$, confirming the Ivančo-Jendrol' conjecture for cubic graphs. The key step is to algorithmically construct a $\{1,n/2+1\}$-vertex labeling such that half of the vertices are labeled $1$ and the average degree of the subgraph induced by them is close enough to two. We extend such a labeling to a total edge irregular $(n/2+1)$-labeling, possibly after a local adjustment to a single vertex.

papers.title: Hand in Silhouette: Synthetic-to-Real Multi-View Hand Reconstruction via Binary Masks
papers.abstract: Calibrated multi-view hand reconstruction has advanced rapidly, yet the effectiveness of existing methods depends strongly on real captured data, which is costly to acquire, limited in hand-geometry diversity, and often affected by imperfect annotations. Synthetic data offers a scalable alternative with accurate supervision, but a substantial synthetic-to-real appearance gap hinders its use. To address this, we introduce Hand in Silhouette (SilHand), a calibrated multi-view hand reconstruction framework that operates on binary hand masks, obtainable at low cost either automatically or manually, to reduce the synthetic-to-real observation gap. Rather than relying on RGB features for 3D lifting, SilHand projects metric 3D hypotheses into each view to query and fuse mask-ray evidence for hand reconstruction. This mask-centric formulation enables training on a large-scale synthetic dataset comprising 46.8k grasping poses and 60k free-hand samples, providing broad coverage of hand geometry while directly transferring to real captured hand geometry. Across five real-world benchmarks, SilHand improves relative reconstruction accuracy from 49.2% to 63.4% using masks rendered from reference hands. Moreover, reconstruction accuracy improves consistently as the synthetic training set grows, indicating that broader geometric coverage translates into better real-world performance. While achieving such diversity is difficult with real captured data, it becomes practical under our mask-centric formulation. Finally, SilHand remains robust under mask corruption, with reconstruction error increasing by at most 1.63 mm. Together, these results support binary masks as an effective interface for learning hand reconstruction from synthetic geometry.

papers.title: The Bolza Surface Does Not Locally Minimize the Diameter Function
papers.abstract: We study the diameter function on the Teichmüller space of closed hyperbolic Riemann surfaces. Although the Bolza surface maximizes the systole among hyperbolic surfaces of genus 2, its extremal behavior with respect to the diameter function is less clear. Using first variations of distances at diameter pairs and linear programming duality, we establish a sufficient criterion for a surface not to be a local minimizer of the diameter function. More precisely, we show that if each diameter pair can be assigned a simple closed geodesic formed by two minimizing geodesic segments joining its endpoints, with distinct assigned geodesics pairwise disjoint, then a deformation varying only the length parameters in Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates strictly decreases the diameter. The assigned geodesics extend to a pants decomposition, and the decrease is detected by a strictly negative upper bound for the first-order variation of the diameter. We then apply this criterion to the Bolza surface and prove that it is not a local minimizer of the diameter function on the Teichmüller space of genus 2.

papers.title: SUMNO: Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates
papers.abstract: Data-driven surrogate modeling has emerged as a powerful paradigm for accelerating computational fluid dynamics, and hierarchical U-shaped networks, which resemble the structure of classical Geometric Multigrid (GMG) methods, have become prevalent designs. Modern surrogates built on these designs achieve competitive accuracy at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers; however, accurate prediction of complex flows remains challenging, and no existing architecture leads across them. In such networks, the multigrid analogy mainly concerns the multi-resolution topology, while their components largely follow common vision practice. To address this, this study introduces SUMNO, a multigrid neural operator for fluid flow fields on regular grids that spatially unrolls a V-cycle into a feed-forward U-shaped network. Parameter-free down- and upsampling stand in for restriction and prolongation, and additive skip connections for coarse-grid correction, with normalization-free transfer and skip pathways. Within this macro-architecture, convolutions are used at the fine and intermediate resolutions and shifted-window attention at the coarsest, whose window partitioning is generalized to handle periodicity independently per axis. Evaluated on unseen test configurations across four unsteady and steady flow benchmarks against five representative baselines, SUMNO is best in 5 of 7 settings and ranks second in the remaining two. It reduces the 10-step rollout MSE by about 30% relative to the strongest baseline, and outperforms three baselines with over 130 million parameters using 9.4 million parameters.

papers.title: HARMONY: an efficient and accurate deep learning framework for prediction of experimental vibrational spectra
papers.abstract: Predicting experimental vibrational spectra requires both efficient molecular calculations and a reliable mapping from theoretical vibrations to measured signals. Here we introduce \textbf{HARMONY}, a two-stage deep-learning framework that bridges this gap using harmonic spectra as physical anchors. Equivariant neural networks directly predict atomic forces and spectroscopic tensors for rapid harmonic-spectrum construction, while HarmoNet combines these spectra with molecular topology and measurement metadata to predict experimental infrared and Raman spectra. HARMONY achieves mean cosine similarities of 0.912 for infrared and 0.907 for Raman spectra, with a mean inference time of 2.12~s per molecule, approximately 600-fold faster than the evaluated DFT workflow. Beyond forward prediction, HARMONY improves inverse molecular inference through pseudo-experimental pretraining and spectral verification of candidate structures. Integrating HARMONY and Vib2Mol as scientific tools within a general-purpose agent enables adaptive candidate generation and verification. With molecular formulas provided, the resulting Vib2Mol--HARMONY Agent achieves Top-1 recall of 70.53\% on NIST using infrared spectra and 83.33\% on SDBS using combined infrared and Raman spectra. Fine-tuning with 19 amino-acid controls and eight peptides further increases mean Raman cosine similarity from 0.669 to 0.896 on 15 held-out peptides. HARMONY establishes harmonic anchoring as a practical connection between molecular physics, experimental spectroscopy and adaptive molecular structure elucidation.

papers.title: Grothendieck groups and Auslander--Reiten relations in extended module categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider Grothendieck groups of extended module categories $\C_m(A)=m\text{-}\modu A$, where $A$ is a finite-dimensional algebra over a field and $m$ is a positive integer. We show that the relation subgroup of the split Grothendieck group of $\C_m(A)$ is generated by Auslander--Reiten extriangles if and only if $\C_m(A)$ has finitely many indecomposable objects up to isomorphism. To this end, we establish a criterion for extriangulated categories with bounded negative extension sequences and a finite extension generator. We then apply this criterion to extended module categories and recover the two-term silting criterion of Padrol, Palu, Pilaud and Plamondon. We also use the cohomological Euler characteristic to determine the rank of the relation subgroup. In particular, when $A$ is hereditary and representation-finite, we explicitly describe the indecomposable objects of $\C_m(A)$ and calculate the rank of its relation subgroup.

papers.title: Strong Well-Posedness and Path-by-Path Uniqueness for Fractional SDEs with Integrable Drifts
papers.abstract: In dimension $d$, we consider stochastic differential equations driven by additive fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H<1/2$ and with a time-dependent drift that is $p$-integrable in space and $q$-integrable in time. Under the subcriticality condition $\frac{Hd}{p}+\frac1q<1-H$, complemented by two integrability conditions needed for Girsanov's theorem, we prove strong existence and path-by-path uniqueness of solutions. We also establish stability with respect to the initial data and the drift, both pathwise and in moment norms, and construct a Hölder continuous semiflow. When $H$ approaches $1/2$, our conditions reduce, up to an endpoint case, to the condition of Krylov and Röckner (2005) for Brownian motion, and in dimension one they complement the results of Nualart and Ouknine (2003), which rely on comparison arguments. Our methods combine the stochastic sewing lemma, Lyons' rough path theory, and the quantitative John--Nirenberg inequality for stochastic processes of vanishing mean oscillation.

papers.title: DRAMA: Dissecting Attention Redundancy for Accelerating Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal diffusion large language models (dLLMs) generate text through iterative masked denoising with bidirectional attention, offering a compelling alternative to autoregressive vision-language modeling. However, each denoising step requires a full forward pass over long multimodal sequences in which visual tokens dominate the sequence length, and a fixed step budget further compounds this quadratic per-step cost. Existing inference acceleration approaches for multimodal dLLMs characterize attention redundancy implicitly, motivating designs from isolated attention visualizations rather than from measurement. We close this gap with DRAMA, a training-free acceleration framework grounded in a systematic dissection of attention redundancy in multimodal dLLMs. By probing attention tensors along spatial and temporal axes, we reveal two persistent redundancy structures: (i) attention mass consistently concentrates on a sparse subset of visual tokens, and (ii) attention distributions rapidly stabilize across denoising steps after an initial formation phase. These findings motivate two complementary mechanisms: Spatial-Redundancy-Aware Visual Token Pruning (SVTP) and Sufficiency-Guided Adaptive Stopping (SGAS). Together, DRAMA achieves an average 18.67 times inference speedup across six vision-language benchmarks without training, architectural modification, or attention caching, while maintaining competitive accuracy. Our results establish a strong, measurement-grounded acceleration baseline for multimodal dLLM inference.

papers.title: MotionSkill: From Bipedal Motion Video to Control across Embodiments
papers.abstract: Reusing a demonstrated gait can reduce the work of specifying the same motion for each biped. A video captures the timing of a step, but each robot must execute it with its own limbs and actuators. MotionSkill recovers a timed reference once from monocular video and adapts it to each target in simulation. It aligns root motion and body landmarks in a common frame and records which landmarks are available at each instant. At each source timestamp, the mapper preserves limb directions, uses the target segment lengths, and solves inverse kinematics under joint limits and closure constraints. In MuJoCo, we train a separate residual policy for each of ten bipeds on its mapped reference from one four-second walking clip. Each policy uses the measured robot state to correct joint commands during contact. From initial states held out during training, MotionSkill completed 98% of trials on the original video and 26% with the upper body occluded for one second.

papers.title: Multi-approach Standard Model Effective Field Theory analyses of top-quark associated production in leptonic final states at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
papers.abstract: Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) interpretations of measurements of top-quark associated production processes in leptonic final states are presented using the full Run 2 proton-proton collision dataset recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. A simultaneous likelihood fit is performed across final states sensitive to $t\bar{t}γ$, $t\bar{t}Z$, $t\bar{t}W$, $t\bar{t}H$, $t\bar{t}t\bar{t}$, $tZq$, $tWZ$, $tHq$, and $tHW$ production, with harmonised reconstructed final-state objects and a coherent treatment of detector-level SMEFT effects across all contributing processes. Two complementary analysis strategies are investigated: an approach employing a more generic event categorisation based on counting reconstructed objects, and a more complex approach combining orthogonal regions optimised to specifically identify individual processes, as employed by previous dedicated measurements. Constraints are obtained on the Wilson coefficients of dimension-six SMEFT operators affecting top-quark interactions, including top-boson, four-quark and top-lepton operators, together with complex operator contributions. The results do not show a significant deviation from the Standard Model expectation and 95% confidence interval limits are placed in a simultaneous fit to 33 SMEFT Wilson coefficients. The comparison of the two analysis strategies provides new insight into the design of increasingly complex SMEFT interpretations. The second, more complex, approach targeting individual processes results in the best sensitivity to the majority of Wilson coefficients.

papers.title: Families of (Pluri)subharmonic Functions and Separate Subharmonicity
papers.abstract: We study the singular sets of pointwise bounded-above envelopes of families of functions. For families of subharmonic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C$, of plurisubharmonic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C^N$, and, more generally, of functions subharmonic in each complex variable separately, we prove that the singular set of a pointwise bounded-above envelope is relatively closed and nowhere dense. In contrast, for $N\ge3$ we construct a sequence of subharmonic functions on $\mathbb R^N$ whose upper envelope is finite everywhere but nowhere locally bounded above. We also characterize the singular sets that arise for admissible classes of functions, both with and without a continuity assumption, and give applications to separately subharmonic functions.

papers.title: An optical-frequency-comb-enabled unified infrastructure for quantum networks
