papers.abstract: Research on pay dispersion has long asked whether unequal rewards increase or depress performance. Tournament theory expects stronger effort, while social comparison accounts expect withdrawal. Both perspectives, however, treat performance as a single scale on which workers can be ranked. Scientific work often resists such ordering. Some contributions extend recognized lines of inquiry and can be evaluated against prevailing standards; others revise the frames through which value is judged and become legible only later. We argue that intellectual tournaments more readily reward the first kind of contribution than the second. Pay dispersion may therefore be associated not only with how much scholars produce but also with what kinds of intellectual exploration are encouraged. We test this argument with administrative payroll records for 105,050 tenure-line faculty in 4,839 departments at 93 U.S. public universities from 2004 to 2026, linked to publication histories in OpenAlex. For each department, we estimate a separate pay equation using rank, contract basis, and seniority, then measure the Gini of the salary variation this local ladder cannot explain. Scholars in departments with greater unexplained pay dispersion publish more papers and receive more citations, but their work is less disruptive, less novel, and more conventional. Additional analyses show that compensation premiums above the ladder go disproportionately to scholars with broad collaborations and topical breadth. Although the design cannot fully separate treatment from selection, the evidence shows that inequality is not only a distributional outcome but also an evaluative structure, shaping which forms of knowledge are recognized, rewarded, and reproduced within organizations and communities.

papers.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
papers.abstract: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair. By identifying and correcting failures, PhysLoop marks a key milestone toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video generation models with limited human intervention. We release 100K videos spanning diverse, realistic indoor and outdoor scenes, along with generation tools and two evaluation datasets: PhysLoop-Gen and PhysLoop-Repair. We evaluate controllable generation and localized repair on these datasets, respectively, and assess physical behavior on the external Physics-IQ Verified benchmark.

papers.title: ORCA:Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment for Multi-View Clustering
papers.abstract: Deep multi-view clustering often suffers from redundant information accumulation during fusion and indiscriminate alignment across representation levels. We propose Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment (ORCA) to address these challenges. Its semantic incremental recurrent fusion module extracts cross-view orthogonal residuals as non-redundant increments and adaptively weights recurrent states through divergence-guided gating. Its consensus-calibrated hierarchical contrastive alignment module uses the global consensus to weight contrastive alignment of view-level, pairwise, and recurrent representations. Together, these modules balance view-specific structure with cross-view consistency. Experiments on five benchmarks against fifteen competing methods demonstrate ORCA's effectiveness, including a 5.25 percent accuracy improvement over the strongest baseline on 100leaves. Ablation studies validate both modules. Code is available at https://github.com/XiaojianDing/2026-NeurIPS-ORCA.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
papers.abstract: Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.

papers.title: Reduced filtering using classical control hierarchy with linear optimality for continuous quantum error correction
papers.abstract: Continuous quantum error correction promises reduced thresholds and hardware overhead compared to the digital paradigm, but its complex model estimation has greatly reduced its practicality. We recast this problem as a classical control-theoretic state hierarchy made of an exact bilinear reduced model, an exact conditional filter, and standard estimation and feedback design. For any $[[n,k,d]]$ stabilizer code whose generators are all continuously monitored and which is driven by a single Pauli recovery channel, we prove that the exact filter closes at dimension $3\cdot2^{\,n-k-1}$. This dimension is set by the syndrome space instead of the Hilbert space and is minimal within invariant-subspace filtering. The reduced model exposes and corrects two failure mechanisms of the feedback loop. Strong monitoring damps the rotational partner through which the controller steers the stabilizer and injects back-action diffusion along the recovery path; lowering the measurement strength during correction raises the entanglement fidelity of partner-steering LQR control by $0.096$ in the three-qubit code with three monitored parities. Linearizing at the codespace leaves the syndrome uncontrollable, so the controller can stall; a gain designed at a shifted operating point removes this degeneracy. In the limit of zero measurement during correction, we prove that a syndrome-only filter is exact at every recovery boundary. The resulting committed-recovery controller needs only $2^{\,n-k}$ class probabilities and gives the highest entanglement fidelity compared among the methods tested in the literature, $0.947$ against $0.920$ for a measurement-based estimator protocol in the three-qubit bit-flip code, and $0.726$ vs at most $0.407$ for continuous controllers in the five-qubit perfect code.

papers.title: AgriSense: Vision-Language Decision Support and Robotic Intervention in a Virtual Greenhouse Copy title
papers.abstract: Autonomous greenhouse management increasingly requires robotic systems that integrate perception, navigation, environmental regulation, and plant-level intervention. This paper presents AgriSense, a framework combining an Isaac Sim virtual greenhouse, a quadruped mobile manipulator, RGB and LiDAR-inertial sensing, environmental control, and supervised vision-language decision support. Frozen DINOv2 and BERT encoders, together with structured environmental inputs, support joint prediction of twelve environmental references, a target zone, and an intervention flag. Checkpoint replay reproduces 41/43 zone decisions. Across five seeds on a source-grouped test set, the full, image-removed, and language-removed configurations each achieve 43/44 correct zone decisions, providing no evidence of incremental multimodal zone-accuracy improvement. The full model achieves mean absolute errors of 0.249 degrees C for temperature, 2.030 percentage points for humidity, and 0.997 percentage points for soil moisture. Sensor-only inputs match full-model zone accuracy, while language-only inputs achieve 68.64%. External real-image benchmarks reveal distribution-shift limitations. Five offline Point-LIO routes yield rigidly aligned trajectory errors of 5.22-17.32 mm. Of 40 virtual-arm targets, 32 satisfy geometric acceptance criteria and eight are rejected at boundaries. Six long-horizon climate cases and fault protocols characterize integration limits. Navigation and integrated treatment rely on simulator-state inputs; physical greenhouse performance and agronomic treatment efficacy remain unvalidated. The contribution is an evaluated decision-support and robotic-intervention framework for a virtual greenhouse.

papers.title: Strong Completeness of Provability Logic for Languages of size at most continuum
papers.abstract: We investigate the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ for an infinite set of propositional variables $\mathbb P$ over ordinal spaces equipped with the interval topology $\mathcal{I}_1$. For every infinite cardinal $κ$, we consider the set \[ Γ_κ= \{\Diamond p_ξ:ξ<κ\} \cup \{\Box(p_ξ\to\Diamond p_η):ξ<η<κ\}, \] and prove that $Γ_κ$ has a model on an ordinal space with $\mathcal{I}_1$ if and only if $κ\nrightarrow_{\mathrm{ipath}}(ω)^2_{ω,<ω}$. We also prove that if $|\mathbb P|<\mathfrak p$, then $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ is strongly complete with respect to $(ω^ω+1,\mathcal I_1)$. Finally, we establish the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ with respect to the same space whenever $|\mathbb P|=\aleph_1$.

papers.title: Existence, Nonexistence, and Regularity Results for Supercritical Quasilinear Elliptic Problems with Hardy Potential
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of solutions to the following supercritical elliptic problem involving the $p$-Laplace operator and the Hardy-Leray potential \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{array}{rcll} -Δ_p u +u^β|\nabla u|^p &= & {\vartheta} \dfrac{u^q }{|x|^p}+ f\;\; &\hbox{in } Ω u &\geq & 0\;\; &\hbox{in } Ω u &= & 0\;\;&\hbox{on } \partialΩ, \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where $0\inΩ$. We analyze the effect of the perturbation term $u^β|\nabla u|^p$, with $β\geq 0$, and the role of the exponent $q$ on the existence of solutions. We also analyze nonexistence of solutions when $f$ is a singular measure. Finally, we focus on the regularity and asymptotic properties of these solutions.

papers.title: A Polynomial-Time Sixth-Power Excluded Grid Theorem
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-time construction for a sixth-power excluded-grid theorem. Every graph whose treewidth is at least $g^6$ times a fixed polylogarithmic factor contains a $g\times g$ grid minor that our randomized algorithm finds with constant probability. The algorithm outputs an explicit minor model, and the exponent in its running time is independent of $g$. This improves the ninth-power existence bound of Chuzhoy and Tan~\cite{CT21} and the $g^{98}$ threshold in the polynomial-time construction of Chekuri and Chuzhoy~\cite{CC16}. Quantitative bounds relating treewidth to grid size are central to bidimensionality, developed by Demaine, Hajiaghayi, and collaborators~\cite{DH05,DH08}. The main ingredient is an asymmetric local routing theorem that uses substantially fewer attachment paths than backbone paths. A balanced recursion preserves connectivity by charging deletions to the boundary of a fixed reference cluster. We construct the smaller attachment sets through a routing hierarchy: either it exposes an accessible well-linked boundary, or its quotient graphs contain the desired grid. These arguments implement cluster splitting using approximate cuts and flow computations. An explicit cut-matching construction and a constructive grid-extraction procedure complete the algorithm. We also give a general packing--covering hypothesis for trees meeting three prescribed terminal sets under which the exponent can be reduced below six. A companion Lean development verifies the new construction, its success guarantee, and the composition of its polynomial running time, using explicit interfaces for the published algorithms and standard finite-data operations.

papers.title: Beyond Binary Classification: Multiclass Machine Learning for Diabetes and Prediabetes Risk Prediction Using NHANES
papers.abstract: Detecting diabetes risk early is important for preventing disease progression. Most existing machine learning approaches focus on binary classification, which limits their ability to capture intermediate risk states such as prediabetes. We develop a supervised learning framework to classify adults as normal, prediabetic, or diabetic using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data. The framework uses routinely collected demographic, clinical, and lifestyle variables from 15,356 adults, with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) used only to define labels and excluded from input features to prevent leakage. We compare conventional machine learning and transformer-based models and examine two binary formulations: normal versus prediabetes, and normal versus combined prediabetes and diabetes. Models are evaluated on a held-out test set using precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. In the multiclass setting, performance is broadly consistent across models, with accuracy up to 0.72 and macro-averaged F1 of 0.70. Prediabetes remains the most challenging class, with F1 scores of 0.54 to 0.56 for conventional models and 0.53 to 0.55 for transformers, reflecting its overlap with both neighboring states. When the task is reduced to normal versus prediabetes, F1 scores rise modestly to 0.62 to 0.64. A more substantial improvement is observed under a broader screening formulation combining prediabetes and diabetes, with F1 scores of 0.73 to 0.74 across all models. These findings suggest that feature overlap along the biological continuum between normal and diabetic states contributes more to the difficulty of prediabetes detection than model architecture. Multiclass prediction provides a more clinically informative representation of metabolic risk progression but highlights a trade-off between clinically meaningful stratification and predictive accuracy.

papers.title: A risk-aware individualized blood pressure target to avoid hypotension in surgery
papers.abstract: We propose an online method for choosing both a blood pressure target and a norepinephrine dose for an individual surgical patient. From a short record of mean arterial pressure (MAP) and norepinephrine delivery, the method fits a reduced pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model and uses a local Gaussian approximation to propagate uncertainty to future MAP readings. It searches for the lowest target for which a bolus and constant infusion keep the predicted probability of at least one MAP reading below 65 mmHg after the rise phase within a prescribed limit. If no such target is found, the decision returns to the clinician. We assess calibration of the predicted minimum MAP on retrospective surgical records under the doses actually administered. In a cohort of 4,096 virtual patients, the method recommended a dose for 74 % of patients at a nominal risk of 5 %. Among the patients receiving a recommendation, 6.9 % had a reading below 65 mmHg. A fixed target of 70 mmHg yielded a rate of 25 % when applied to the full virtual cohort.

papers.title: Tracking relevance syntactically: A nested approach to weak relevant logic
papers.abstract: The variable-sharing property (VSP) is regarded as a key feature of relevant logics, while the Craig interpolation property (CIP), formulated with respect to relevant implication, implies the VSP in constant-free propositional languages. However, to the best of our knowledge, no constant-free distributive relevant logic has previously been shown to enjoy the CIP. This absence of positive results has contributed to a widespread impression among relevant logicians that relevance and Craig interpolation are incompatible. In this work, we address this tension by proving that the negation-free fragment of base relevant logic B, denoted B+, enjoys both properties. Our proof is purely syntactic and is based on a novel nested sequent calculus featuring binary relevant blocks as primitive structural constructs. Unlike conventional nested sequent calculi, where unary nesting reflects the binary accessibility relation of Kripke semantics, our calculus employs a binary nesting operator that directly reflects the ternary relational structure of Routley-Meyer semantics for relevant logics. After establishing soundness and cut-free completeness of the calculus, we prove several meta-logical properties for the logic. Most notably, we provide the first syntactic proof of the VSP (along with a variety of its stronger variants) and the first proof of the CIP for B+, both derived directly from the cut-free system using a structural notion internalized within nested sequents.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic without tests does not have Craig Interpolation
papers.abstract: It was shown recently by Borzechowski et al. (2026) that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has Craig Interpolation. Whether test-free PDL, i.e. PDL without the `?' operator, has interpolation remained open. Here we answer this question in the negative with a counterexample: a test-free PDL validity for which no test-free interpolant exists. The validity only uses one atomic program and the Kleene star, so it implies that the basic modal logic K extended with the reflexive transitive closure does not have interpolation, as previously shown by Studer (2009). The example was originally obtained using LLMs and Lean. We describe our methodology and provide links to all prompts, LLM output summaries as well as the Lean proof.

papers.title: Global climate modeling of the Martian water cycle. I) Improved parameterizations of physical processes
papers.abstract: We implement four new physical parameterizations relevant to the water cycle in the Mars PCM (previously Mars Laboratoire de M{é}t{é}orologie Dynamique GCM)\,: the latent heat of ground ice sublimation, a temperature-dependent nucleation scheme in cloud microphysics, differentiated albedos for water frost and perennial ice and scavenging of water ice clouds by CO2 particle formation. After a new tuning of the poorly known model parameters, we find that combining these parameterizations allows for an improved agreement of the modeled water cycle compared to Thermal Emission Spectrometer column-integrated vapor and ice retrievals. We show that latent heat cooling prevents the formation of surface liquid water at present and likely in the recent past on Mars. Using two albedos corrects the overestimation of the northern sublimation event, a major defect of the model. Our study highlights that each parameterization has indirect consequences amplified by the radiatively active clouds. We stress that the increasingly complex water cycle in the Mars PCM should be studied in the future using numerical methods tailored for climate modeling, in addition to the effect of each individual component.

papers.title: Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
papers.abstract: We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $ν^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $ν$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-rν^{\frac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-νt}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim ν^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $ν$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$.

papers.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
papers.abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with Hölder-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the Hölder topology.

papers.title: Composition loci, invariant Bezoutians, and finite-orbit correspondences
papers.abstract: We compute projective degrees of composition loci for polynomial and rational maps of the projective line. For normalized polynomials of degree $rs$ with a right composition factor of degree $s$, a projective-bundle construction gives the degree $S(r+s-2,r)$. We extend this calculation to composition chains, and obtain $S(r+s-1,r)$ in the uncentered normalization used for decomposable interpolation. For rational maps, a Grassmann-bundle model gives a Plücker degree formula and an interpretation by prescribed critical points. We relate these loci to factorization of the Bezoutian in the ring of symmetric polynomials, where factors correspond to monodromy orbits on unordered pairs. Fried's polynomial criterion then determines the invariant reducibility locus. For rational maps we determine its composition components when a marked pole fiber has exactly one ramified point and at least one unramified point. The qualitative equivalence between finite full orbits and a first integral is already known. We give a direct proof from forward stabilization, with an explicit test using bounded forward orbits and with quotient fibers identified at every point. We also determine when absolute and invariant irreducibility differ and give a growth formula for a class of translation correspondences.

papers.title: Efficient Periocular Recognition through Model Scaling and Cross Spectral VIS NIR Verification
papers.abstract: Periocular recognition offers an efficient alternative to full-face verification when facial regions are occluded or image resolution is limited. We present AdaEye, a systematic study of input and backbone scaling for periocular verification in visible-spectrum (VIS) and cross-spectral (VIS/NIR) settings. Using an AdaFace-style framework, we compare full-face, masked-face, and dedicated 80x40 periocular inputs while varying backbone width and embedding dimensionality. Across four VIS/VIS and VIS/NIR protocols, we assess verification accuracy, computational cost, inference throughput, training memory, template size, and training stability. Direct periocular processing reduces recognition cost from 6.30 to 1.64 GMACs per image and increases measured throughput by approximately threefold. Its effectiveness depends on the evaluation protocol: periocular models perform better on native UFPR periocular images, whereas face-based protocols favor retaining more input information. Moderate backbone width reductions maintain comparable mean verification performance on CASIA and ND-NIVL while reducing computation. Embedding compression decreases template-storage requirements, primarily benefiting deployment. Multi-seed experiments reveal that some configurations require numerical stabilization, particularly when embedding and backbone reductions are combined. These findings support selecting compact periocular architectures according to the target protocol and deployment constraints, balancing accuracy, efficiency, storage, and robustness.

papers.title: Physical interpretation of spin-glass models with correlated disorder
papers.abstract: Ising spin-glass models with a specific type of correlated bond disorder have recently been used to relate properties of spin-glass phases, such as temperature chaos and magnetic-field chaos, to ferromagnetic order. This correlated disorder has a simple physical interpretation, which underlies the sampling procedure introduced by Oshima, Arai, and Hukushima for numerical simulations: the bond configuration is obtained from the Edwards-Anderson model with the symmetric $\pm J$ distribution by drawing one of its equilibrium spin configurations and writing the model in the gauge in which this reference configuration becomes the all-up state. The construction is analogous to the Mattis model, with the roles of the ferromagnet and the spin glass reversed: whereas the Mattis model is a ferromagnet in disguise, the ferromagnetic phase of the correlated model is essentially a spin-glass phase in disguise. The frustration statistics of the correlated-disorder model are exactly those of the symmetric $\pm J$ model, and, in a generalization with an additional parameter $γ$, the probabilities of the gauge equivalence classes are determined by $γ$ alone, whereas the inverse temperature at which the reference configuration is drawn determines only the distribution within each class. The magnetization of this model is the overlap with the reference configuration. Through this correspondence, studies of its ferromagnetic phase have led to unexpected results on temperature chaos and magnetic-field chaos in the spin-glass phase of the Edwards-Anderson model. Models with correlated disorder have thus provided a new perspective on spin glasses and have proved fertile ground for highly nontrivial results on the spin-glass problem.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Persistence in NISP detectors
papers.abstract: Detector persistence is a significant source of systematic error in infrared observations and affects the scientific performance of the \Euclid Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP). We characterise persistence using complementary ground calibration and in-flight data, develop empirical models of its temporal evolution, and assess its impact on science observations and the \Euclid data-processing pipeline. Persistence is highly non-uniform across the focal plane, with variations of up to two orders of magnitude between and within detectors. Its amplitude is typically below 1\% of the stimulus signal and depends nonlinearly on the preceding fluence. The decay rate is faster for brighter sources. During mission operations, the persistence signal has progressively decreased by roughly 10\%, while the decay rate has remained approximately stable. Persistence following over-saturating signals does not follow the empirical relations derived for under-saturating fluences and plausibly reduces persistence response over longer timescales. The impact of charge trapping and release on flat-field observations and on the background in science exposures is also discussed. Persistence measured in science observations is observed to differ systematically from that derived from dark calibration data. In addition, persistence of energetic particle hits is observed to be different from that of astronomical sources of comparable signal. Finally, we discuss the impact of persistence on \Euclid NISP observations and describe the masking strategy adopted for the Q1 abd DR1 releases, focusing on identifying which pixels are affected by persistence and for how long they should be excluded from science observations.

papers.title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. While recent benchmarks have begun assessing these models on driving scenes, they mainly target routine traffic conditions and general comprehension tasks based on existing driving datasets and therefore fail to evaluate model performance on the rarest and most safety-critical driving events, also known as "corner cases". To provide a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs on precisely these scenarios, we introduce DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 carefully curated driving videos spanning not only collision-related corner cases but also rare non-collision ones. Through extensive prompts and open-ended question answering, we expose a critical capability gap: all evaluated models perform substantially below the threshold required for safety-critical driving applications, frequently misjudging or missing dangerous events on the road ahead and hallucinating non-existent agents or actions in their explanations. We believe DashBench, combining an extensive dataset with a rigorous evaluation toolkit and a detailed diagnosis of current model limitations, drives progress toward safer, more explainable autonomous driving systems. The code and data will be shared at: cornercase-dashbench.github.io

papers.title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values
papers.abstract: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.

papers.title: On the randomized lattice-point count problem
papers.abstract: Counting (integer) lattice points in a convex body $K$ has a rich history, beginning with the famous circle problem imposed by Gauss in 1834. Clearly, the number of covered lattice points depends on the position, orientation, size, and shape of $K$ in a delicate way. In 1947, Kendall was the first to consider a randomized version of this problem by allowing random translations of $K$. In this survey, we aim to provide an overview of the current state of research on the \emph{randomized lattice-point count problem}, i.e.\ on the distribution of the lattice-point count under random rotations and translations of $K$. As it turns out, even the variance is far from being well-understood, leaving multiple open questions for future research. The motivation for the present work grew out of the author's research interest in a related combinatorial problem, dealing with the convex hull of all covered lattice points.

papers.title: Understanding the normal state of cuprate superconductors
papers.abstract: Doped holes in the CuO2 planes reside pairwise at O atoms. Their lack of net charge demotes the flanking Cu3d-O2p holes of half-filling. Below the doping-dependent pseudogap (PG) temperature, the latter are trapped between motted Cu2+ ions. Above the PG temperature, the remaining Cu3d-O2p holes are thermally demotted, initiating the strange metal (SM) phase. The PG energy at the antinodal points in the BZ decreases with increasing doping, as less Cu3d-O2p holes need to be thermally demotted. In the SM phase, the Cu3d-O2p holes hop, with Planckian scattering rate, by leaps of lattice-constant length. This gives rise to a linear resistivity. O atoms in the CuO2 plane, from Sr doping of 214 cuprates or from oxygen enrichment (OE), arrange to a charge order (CO). In 214 systems, an O superlattice (SL) forms of increasing incommensurability with doping. It saturates when a secondary SL forms. At the quantum critical point their incommensurabilities equal, causing collapse of the PG temperature. In OE cuprates, the CO dilutes the diagonal tilt of the host lattice CuO6 octahedra, causing a decreasing incommensurability with doping. Oxygen atoms are singlets in OE cuprates but triplets in 214 systems. The magnetic moment of the latter gives rise to a narrow 3D AFM doping range and to magnetic order accompanying CO (stripes). Charge-density fluctuations occur when double holes hop back and forth between O atoms of the SL and neighboring oxygen ions. Quantum oscillations result from Fermi surface reconstruction.

papers.title: Inertial modes in a turbulent rotating magneto-convection simulation with the solar-like differential rotation
papers.abstract: Recent observations have revealed a variety of solar inertial modes, but their nonlinear properties remain largely unexplored. We aim to identify and characterize inertial modes in a state-of-the-art simulation of rotating magnetoconvection, in which solar-like differential rotation was self-consistently reproduced. We analyzed nine years of high-cadence data from the Hotta (2025) simulation. The spatial eigenfunctions of various low-frequency inertial modes were extracted using singular value decomposition. We identified major classes of retrograde inertial modes, including equatorial Rossby modes, high-latitude modes, and high-frequency retrograde modes, with frequencies and near-surface amplitudes roughly consistent with the solar observations. In particular, thanks to the strongly baroclinic background in the simulation, the observed large amplitude ($\sim 10$ m/s) and the characteristic polar spiral pattern of the high-latitude mode at azimuthal order $m=1$ are successfully reproduced. This indicates that high-latitude modes are excited by baroclinic instability, which can occur even amid turbulent convection. We further show that the prograde columnar modes undergo a qualitative transition at $m \sim 6$, separating the fast-propagating convective modes at $m \gtrsim 6$ from thermally diffusive slow modes at $m \lesssim 6$ whose frequencies closely match recent observational inferences of thermal Rossby modes. Finally, we find that turbulent magnetic fields primarily influence the inertial modes indirectly through modifications of the background state. Our results suggest that the observed properties of solar inertial modes are broadly consistent with a simulation in which solar-like differential rotation is maintained in a magnetically dominated regime, although the simulation still overproduces prograde columnar modes at large $m$.

papers.title: Class-Competence Aggregation: Output-Layer Routing for Federated Multiclass DDoS Detection under Class-Concentrated Non-IID Data
papers.abstract: Federated learning over distributed intrusion-detection sensors naturally produces \emph{class-concentrated} non-IID data, where an entire attack class is held by a single client and absent elsewhere. We show this collapses federated averaging in a specific, localized way: the output layer holds one decision boundary per class, and when a class's aggregation weight comes overwhelmingly from clients that have never seen it, its neuron receives an active anti-signal rather than mere dilution, collapsing to zero. On CIC-DDoS2019, standard FedAvg drives the concentrated LDAP class to $0.00 \pm 0.00\%$ F1 across every seed. We propose Class-Competence Aggregation (CCA), which aggregates the output layer per class using each client's own locally reported validation F1 as the weight, while hidden layers remain under standard size-weighted FedAvg. CCA requires no server-held auxiliary data and adds only one F1 scalar per class per round beyond the feature-scaling and class-count exchanges common to any federated pipeline. On our primary CNN-LSTM architecture, CCA alone raises LDAP F1 from $0\%$ to $84.83 \pm 1.65\%$, and the full method reaches $91.64 \pm 0.57\%$ macro F1, closing the federated-to-centralized gap from $-42.53$ to $-4.05$ points. Benchmarked against four other federated methods under identical partitions and seeds, CCA is the only one that recovers the concentrated class substantially and reliably; a $178\times$ smaller MLP shows the same qualitative recovery, though less completely, confirming the effect holds across architecture scale even as its magnitude varies. Results are validated across three seeds and replicated on a second dataset, CICIDS2017.

papers.title: Large Pockels Effect in Multiaxial Ferroelectrics Induced by Polarization Reorientation
papers.abstract: Materials with large linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect have significant potential for fabricating energy-efficient photonic devices. Previous strategies have mostly relied on structural softness---associated with phase boundary, domain wall, or strain induced phase transition---to create large Pockels effect in ferroelectrics. In this Letter, we show that polarization reorientation in multiaxial ferroelectrics may create structural softness and thus induce large Pockels effect. By developing a phenomenological theory, we find that multiaxial ferroelectrics exhibit a hysteretic relationship between the azimuth angles of the polarization and the electric field, and a possible divergence of the linear electro-optic coefficient may occur at an appropriate polarization azimuth angle. This suggests a brand-new strategy for engineering large Pockels effect in multiaxial ferroelectrics. We perform first-principles simulations on several multiaxial ferroelectrics and predict that polarization reorientation can significantly enhance the electro-optic coefficients in monolayer SnSe and bulk KNbO$_3$. This validates the soundness of our strategy and emphasizes multiaxial ferroelectrics as promising platforms toward large Pockels effect.

papers.title: Inter-city 18.9 km free-space QKD over a dense urban corridor
papers.abstract: Terrestrial free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) provides a flexible complement to fiber-based networks, but its deployment over long horizontal paths in dense metropolitan environments remains challenging, as atmospheric turbulence, demanding pointing and tracking requirements, and operational constraints can substantially increase system complexity. We experimentally demonstrate the operation of a decoy-state BB84 system over an 18.9~km free-space link across a densely populated urban area in the metropolitan region of Barcelona using an aviation-compliant optical architecture. The system operates at 785~nm using room-temperature single-photon detectors and requires no adaptive optics at the receiver. The modular QKD transmitter, based on a deployment-oriented design, is interfaced with a versatile free-space optical terminal and an independent GPS-disciplined synchronization architecture, facilitating its integration into heterogeneous optical infrastructures. We present the transmitter performance and optical-link characteristics, together with a 40-minute field test characterized by an average channel attenuation of approximately 19~dB and a mean QBER of 1.31\%. From the measured channel parameters, we estimate an average finite-size secret key rate exceeding 11~kbit/s. These results demonstrate the feasibility of inter-city free-space QKD over dense urban areas using a comparatively simple architecture.

papers.title: Novel upper bounds for Borsuk numbers from contact points and spherical partitions
papers.abstract: Let $b(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every bounded set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of positive diameter can be partitioned into $m$ sets of smaller diameter. We prove that \[ b(4)\le6,\qquad b(5)\le12,\qquad b(6)\le31,\qquad b(7)\le45,\qquad b(8)\le89, \] and that \[ b(n)\le1+2^{n-1}\left(\tfrac{39}{64}\right)^{\lfloor(n-1)/8\rfloor} \qquad\text{for every } n\ge9 ; \] for instance, $b(9)\le157$ and $b(17)\le24337$. Further constructions give, for example, $b(10)\le289$ and $b(13)\le2313$. These bounds improve Lassak's bound $b(n)\le2^{n-1}+1$ of 1982 in every dimension $n\ge4$. In dimension four they also improve the recent bounds $b(4)\le8$ (Tolmachev and Voronov, May 2026) and $b(4)\le7$ (Arman, Bondarenko, Prymak and Radchenko, October 2026); the bound $b(4)\le6$ was announced independently by Chalmers in November 2026. The bounds for $n\ge7$ have analytic proofs: a quantitative form of Lassak's reduction to coverings of the sphere is combined with normal partitions of weighted vector configurations, for which the smallest inner product within a region is estimated explicitly. The bound for $n=6$ uses a covering of $S^4$ by thirty sets, checked in rational arithmetic. For $n=4,5$ three contact points of the circumscribed ball reduce the problem to a four-parameter family of bodies, which is split by finitely many power diagrams; that all parts have diameter less than one is verified by a computer program with rigorous error control.

papers.title: Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
papers.abstract: Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, we compare key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. In this comparison, we fix the finite field, terminal set, and wiretap family. Each edge supplies one independent uniform symbol to its endpoints for key relay, or carries one symbol once for network coding. The network code may choose its source terminal, edge orientations, and causal transmission order before execution. In this setting, the standard one-time-pad simulation readily converts every secure network code to key relay. We investigate the reverse conversion to linear network coding. For two terminals and a one-symbol key, arbitrary key relay is equivalent to scalar linear acyclic network coding over the prescribed field. The proof uses connectivity and flow conservation, related to the binary $st$-flow protocol. However, this equivalence fails in general when several terminals seek one common key. A doubled triangle separates key relay from acyclic coding but admits causal coding on a cyclic orientation. On the four-terminal complete graph, a linear key relay protocol over the ternary field withstands the three perfect-matching wiretap sets, whereas no linear causal network code distributes a source symbol of the same size, even with private randomness at every vertex and its use in decoding. We also establish a linear key relay normal form that removes interaction and private randomness and bounds public communication. All results concern one-shot feasibility with exact agreement and perfect secrecy.

papers.title: Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fréchet differentiability
papers.abstract: We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fréchet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Tišer. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fréchet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.

papers.title: Data-Driven Robust Inventory Planning and Advertising under Product Return
papers.abstract: Online advertising is a central marketing lever for e-commerce retailers, yet it complicates operational planning by simultaneously stimulating product demand and increasing product returns. Motivated by the practice of a fashion retailer on Amazon, we study a retailer's joint inventory and advertising problem across multiple products over a single season, in which advertising has both direct and cross-product spillover effects on demand and returns. Using linear net-demand and return models that capture both effects, we formulate a contextual stochastic optimization model that jointly determines inventory levels and advertising decisions before the selling season. Because ad clicks are realized only after the advertising decision, the predictive covariates are partially observable and decision-dependent, and their joint distribution with the demand and return errors is unknown. We therefore develop an estimate-then-robustify (ETR) approach grounded in a data-driven robust satisficing framework. We establish a finite-sample guarantee on the out-of-sample profit of the ETR solution that holds for any parameter estimator, show that the solution is asymptotically optimal when the estimator is consistent and the profit target approaches the empirical optimal profit, and derive a mixed-integer conic approximation via affine recourse adaptation that is exact for a single product. On the retailer's data, ETR improves out-of-sample profit over conventional estimate-then-optimize by 6.39\% and earns the higher profit in 74.5% of instances, with the largest gains when training data are scarce; the gain falls to 1.02% when the decision model omits cross-product spillovers.

papers.title: Computation with Backward Feedback: Power, Observation, and Cost
papers.abstract: How much can a computation gain by passing information back to an earlier stage, and how soon can an observer obtain the answer? We study deterministic programs whose runs are accessed at randomly selected stages. A program keeps a register, a finite block of memory. A random clock selects the current stage; each tick takes a random step, with a law fixed independently of input, program and register. When the clock moves backward, the register contents at the stage it leaves start a new run, and the clock continues where it lands. Equilibrium readout requires a distribution of clock position and register that one tick leaves unchanged, and a correct final answer under every such distribution. For bounded steps in both directions with negative average, we obtain an exact classification at each polynomial scale s. If running time and register length are both O(s), feedback gives exactly nondeterministic space O(s); without transmission the class is deterministic time O(s), which is strictly smaller. An observer that starts at stage zero with an all-zero register, reads sequentially and never accepts a nonmember sees, with fewer ticks than any exponential, only languages fixed by a bounded input prefix. Exponentially many ticks reveal every linear-time language. For a clock moving one step up or down, we bound the wait for useful backward moves and the rate of random erasures a stored counter tolerates. The results separate the power of feedback at equilibrium, observation from a fixed start, and the cost of obtaining and keeping information.

papers.title: Learning to control and predict light-driven electron-phonon dynamics
papers.abstract: Driving lattice vibrations provides a direct route to manipulating electronic correlations through nonlinear electron-phonon coupling. Finding suitable driving fields, however, requires control over the coupled dynamics beyond a simple choice of pulse amplitude and frequency. Here we develop a differentiable framework that combines field optimization with neural-network prediction in a two-site electron-phonon model. We compare piecewise-constant, B-spline, feed-forward, and recurrent control parameterizations, optimized to increase the accumulated electronic double occupation. For the dissipation-free model at zero Hubbard interaction, all the methods increase double occupation, with the B-spline raising the mean total double occupation of approximately 30%. Alongside control optimization, a separate recurrent network learns to predict the next-step double occupation and phonon observables from their preceding values and the applied field. These results establish a computational proof of concept for shaping local electronic correlations through a phonon drive and identify a promising route toward learned models for nonequilibrium materials control.

papers.title: Boundary Actuation of a Chain Fountain - Physically Admissible Tracking, Stochastic Limits and Zero-Gravity Circulation
papers.abstract: This paper was inspired by a post on Twitter and by the eight months the author spent at the AASS Centre at Orebro University in 2007. This phenomenon is interesting not only to a physicist, but also to someone like me working in control theory, because of its potential relevance to stabilizing drones and similar flying machines subject to random velocity fluctuations while hovering. A chain fountain can settle without an engineered controller, yet its natural height is selected by transport and boundary forces. We ask how an ideal boundary traction force can sustain a prescribed height or motion. Within an established three-state model, we connect feedback design to force and energy balances and derive sufficient conditions for nominal tracking that preserve the model's mechanical constraints. We also bound the deviations caused by bounded pickup uncertainty. The resulting framework explains how feedback can shape a naturally regulated process and identifies physical limits on the motions it can sustain: stabilizing a mathematical trajectory is useful only if the corresponding motion remains mechanically admissible. This is a preliminary step towards stabilization of the chain in three dimensions.

papers.title: Combining TTVs, RVs, and astrometry to characterize distant giant companions of transiting hot Jupiters: Application to WASP-4
papers.abstract: The origins and architectures of hot Jupiter (HJ) systems remain unclear, with potential explanations for the tight orbits being in-situ formation, disk-migration, or high-eccentricity migration. These mechanisms can leave different imprints on the orbital architecture, but tidal interactions act to erase these imprints for HJs, leading to orbital circularization, realignment, and potentially orbital decay. The latter can be mimicked by the introduction of light travel-time effects (LTTE) caused by an outer giant companion, as for WASP-4$\,$b. We examine the WASP-4 system using newly obtained ESO$\,$3.6/HARPS radial velocity (RV) observations and archival transit-timing data, leveraging the LTTE. Furthermore, we present a novel approach of analyzing HJ systems in sight of $\textit{Gaia}$'s Data Release 4. We propose combining RV, transit-timing, and astrometry data, making use of the LTTE as a proxy for the orbital motion of a possible outer companion. We combine and fit all currently available data and simulate $\textit{Gaia}$ DR4 and DR5 astrometric measurements of WASP-4 and perform an injection and recovery procedure to estimate their impact on the recovered planetary parameters of WASP-4$\,$c. The procedure employs a combined model that describes RVs, transit timing variations (TTVs) via the LTTE, and astrometry simultaneously. Analyzing the existing data, we improve the planetary parameters of WASP-4$\,$c, finding a minimum mass of $9.3\pm1.7\,M_\mathrm{Jup}$ with an orbital period of $10\,600^{+1100}_{-1000}\,$d, or about $29\,$yr. Furthermore, we find that there is no significant orbital decay taking place for WASP-4$\,$b. In simulations of $\textit{Gaia}$ DR5, our three-pronged approach reduces the error bars of WASP-4$\,$c's parameters by about $10\%$, $25\%$, and $33\%$ for its orbital period, time of inferior conjunction, and RV semi-amplitude, respectively. (abridged)

papers.title: The Same But Different: SiO$_2$ Clouds in Two L-Dwarfs with JWST
papers.abstract: The precision of brown dwarf spectra from JWST enables unprecedented insight into the atmospheric and cloud properties of sub-stellar atmospheres. Here, we compare both self-consistent radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) and retrieval atmosphere models to high-SNR 1--18~$μ$m spectra of two field L-dwarfs from JWST, J0624 (L5) and J2148 (L6--L6.5). Our observations include spectral features from H$_2$O, CO, CO$_2$, CH$_4$, Na, and K and cover approximately 98\% of the outgoing thermal emission from the two objects. We first compare the data to three independent grids of 1D-RCE models: BT-Settl, exoREM, and Sonora Diamondback. While exoREM provides the best fit of the grid models, no 1D-RCE model provides a satisfactory fit to the data, highlighting the complexity of fitting cloudy L-dwarf spectra. Nonetheless, the temperature and cloud properties can be constrained with the 1D-RCE models, while metallicity, C/O ratio, and surface gravity are not well-measured. Next, we use petitRADTRANS to retrieve atmosphere and cloud properties, finding strong evidence for the presence of SiO$_2$ clouds in both objects. The SiO$_2$ is found to be amorphous in structure for J0624 but crystalline in J2148, highlighting important differences in objects of similar spectral type. We also used a non-Bayesian optimization framework to explore a wider variety of cloud scenarios, finding evidence for the inclusion of iron-rich magnesium silicates (Mg$_{0.5}$Fe$_{0.5}$SiO$_3$, MgFeSiO$_4$) in addition to SiO$_2$ in both objects. These results show both the complexity and diversity of brown dwarf cloud properties, while also highlighting the constraining power of broad-wavelength JWST observations of cloudy L-dwarfs.

papers.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.

papers.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $σ/m_χ\sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $σ/m_χ= 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_χ\simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_χ\simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

papers.title: RadarML: A Multi-Channel Over-the-Air Dataset of Common Radar Waveforms for ES Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "RadarML", a publicly available dataset of modulated radar pulses recorded over-the-air across multiple semi-independent receiver channels. The dataset was generated using the UCL ARESTOR platform which is a Radio Frequency System on a Chip (RFSoC) based Software Defined Radio (SDR). The dataset contains a library of around two million waveforms with varying centre frequencies, bandwidths, pulse widths and modulations, with 1,000 examples of each signal variation per receiver channel. The goal of this dataset is to enable comparative analysis of radar modulation classification techniques on real data and stimulate research into multi-channel signal detection and modulation classification methods.

papers.title: MESH: Multi-receiver Evaluation of Spatial Hearing across Egocentric and Allocentric Views
papers.abstract: Spatial hearing in multi-receiver environments requires identifying who speaks, where they are, and how they move. Existing benchmarks evaluate spatial prediction, transcription, tracking, and distributed speech processing, but offer limited evaluation of whether speech signal remains associated with the correct physical source across receivers and motion. We introduce MESH, which evaluates this association through egocentric and allocentric views of shared acoustic scenes. The egocentric view uses local recordings and peer metadata, while the allocentric view combines synchronized recordings from multiple receivers in a shared 3D world frame. MESH contains nearly 40,000 questions across 13 static and dynamic localization and spatial transcription tasks. We evaluate eleven audio-model configurations and a language-model agent using specialist tools. The best static distance-estimation and dynamic direction-tracking accuracies are only 21.90% and 41.54%, respectively, while the lowest word error rates across four transcription tasks range from 59.15% to 73.10%. Ablation studies and additional experiments reveal that existing models are not yet able to effectively leverage peer information and struggle to handle multi-speaker and dynamic scenarios. These findings highlight the gap between access to distributed acoustic information and its effective use for spatial speech understanding. We release the dataset and evaluation code to support further research on collaborative and distributed spatial hearing.

papers.title: Enabling Mie Resonances for Optomagnetism in Epitaxially Grown Garnet Nanodisks via Photonic Crystals
papers.abstract: An all-garnet photonic-crystal substrate compatible with epitaxial growth on gadolinium gallium garnet is proposed for controlling the optomagnetic response of a single bismuth iron garnet nanodisk. The photonic environment modifies the spectral positions and relative strengths of the electric- and magnetic-dipole contributions and redistributes the optical field inside the disk. Compared with a reference nanodisk on a homogeneous substrate evaluated near the broad maximum of its summed multipolar response, the peak axial optical contribution to the inverse Faraday effect in the examined cross-sections is enhanced by factors of approximately 7.3 and 6.3 in the magnetic- and electric-dipole-dominated regimes, respectively. The enhancement reaches approximately 7.9 at the maximum of the summed multipolar scattering contributions. These results demonstrate spectral control of the magnitude and spatial distribution of the local optomagnetic response through the photonic environment, without changing the nanodisk geometry.

papers.title: ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes
papers.abstract: The growing volume of process data generated by screwdriving systems, combined with advancements in computing power, data storage, and algorithms, is facilitating the application of artificial intelligence in this field. Accurately detecting and classifying screwdriving errors is crucial for ensuring product quality, avoiding costly rework in manufacturing, and supporting sustainability by facilitating the maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products. In this context, machine learning approaches offer a promising alternative to traditional monitoring techniques, such as window-based methods or envelope curves. This study examines the use of deep learning techniques for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving processes. The data corpus consists of multivariate time series capturing process parameters, such as torque and rotation angle. For anomaly detection, the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder was analyzed. In terms of error classification, four different model architectures were evaluated. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection and confirm that deep learning models can distinguish between multiple error categories beyond traditional binary classification. This extends the capabilities of conventional monitoring approaches, achieving accuracies of up to 100%. Additionally, real-world data material was examined in order to further demonstrate model robustness. Overall the results indicate strong generalization capability and highlight the practical potential of the developed models for use in industrial screwdriving processes, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in error identification and significantly reducing manual effort and analysis time.

papers.title: Parameter estimation in models with explosive drift and Gaussian noise
papers.abstract: We study drift parameter estimation for a positive stochastic process with singular mean-reverting drift driven by Gaussian noise. For Riemann-Liouville fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $H>1/2$, an observable fractional transformation reduces the model to a semimartingale with drift linear in the unknown parameters. Using the quasi-likelihood approach, we derive explicit estimators of both drift coefficients. For a broader class of Gaussian driving processes, we construct a strongly consistent estimator of the ratio $a/b$, which has a natural mean-reversion interpretation, and verify the required assumptions for several Gaussian models. The theoretical results are complemented by a simulation study investigating the effects of the observation horizon and the discretization step on the finite-sample accuracy of the proposed estimators.

papers.title: Non-Convex Optimization via Quantum Tunneling Search on a Photonic Chip
papers.abstract: Non-convex optimization plays an important role in modern machine learning since plenty of real-world problems have objective functions or constraints with non-convex properties. The non-convex nature of landscapes gives rise to numerous local minima and saddle points, dramatically hindering the ability of gradient descent-based methods to explore the landscape and obtain global optima. Here we present quantum tunneling search (QTS), an algorithm based on quantum tunneling walk and local annealing, which effectively explores the non-convex landscape by leveraging the quantum tunneling effect. In experiments, we map an objective function to the potential term of the waveguide Hamiltonian by controlling the refractive index with the femtosecond direct laser writing technique. With a proper input state, the average probability distributions on 10-micrometer-spaced 29 x 1 and 21 x 9 waveguide arrays highlight the local minima of various 1D and 2D non-convex landscapes, respectively. By further introducing the varying Hamiltonian approach, more efficient search and even the identification of the global minimum are achieved. Our work experimentally verifies that QTS is a successful and efficient non-convex optimization solver, demonstrating quantum speedups over classical stochastic gradient descent (SGD), which serves as a practical application of near-term analog quantum simulators in the field of machine learning.

papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties. Our results show that the effectiveness of data acquisition strategies depend strongly on the interplay between the model, dataset, and prediction task, although uncertainty-based sampling generally outperforms alternative strategies. Based on these findings, we derive guidelines for selecting data acquisition strategies under a given labelling budget.

papers.title: EG360: Efficient and Generalizable $360^\circ$ Depth Estimation via Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation and Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion
papers.abstract: Generalized panorama depth estimation has witnessed great advances in recent years. These methods typically achieve robust zero-shot generalization performance using large pretrained models, but their high computational cost makes real-time inference on embedded platforms challenging. In contrast, previous lightweight panorama models have mostly been developed for single-domain evaluations and cannot generalize well due to domain shifts. To reduce the gap between these two types of models, we introduce EG360, an efficient and generalizable panorama depth estimation model. Specifically, building on a lightweight depth model, we design an Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation (APPD) strategy guided by scene geometry, along with a Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion (SCFF) module for global semantic perception. As a result, with only 6.593M parameters after reparameterization, EG360 achieves strong zero-shot performance on real-world benchmarks and runs at 35 FPS on a Jetson Orin NX 16GB in MAXN mode, whereas a previous ViT-small model runs at less than 2 FPS. Our code will also be made public for future research.

papers.title: Hong$-$Ou$-$Mandel-like interference between two independent narrowband thermal states
papers.abstract: Narrowband photonic sources are promising candidates in quantum networks for a direct interface with atomic quantum memories. However, building a large-scale quantum network requires many indistinguishable sources, and matching the frequencies of independent narrowband sources is generally challenging. Here, we propose a method to measure the frequency difference between two narrowband light sources in the single-photon power regime by studying Hong$-$Ou$-$Mandel-like (HOM) interference between thermal states. Our results show that the absolute value of the frequency difference can be extracted from the temporal coincidence counts, and these results agree well with our theoretical model. We also demonstrate that the beat signal of the HOM-like interference between two thermal states has a similar oscillation profile to the HOM interference between two heralded single-photon sources, confirming that this method can be used to find the zero detuning of two heralded single-photon sources.

papers.title: KuaiRecV2: Benchmarking Large-Scale Continual Learning for Diversified and Multi-task Recommendation
papers.abstract: Recommender systems, which retrieve items of interest to users based on their interaction histories, have recently witnessed several key technological advancements, benefiting from the semantic representation space and model-data scaling. Nevertheless, practitioners and researchers have frequently encountered critical inconsistencies between simple offline evaluations and complex online results, and this gap still exists in the era of large models. In this work, we address several key factors that contribute to this inconsistency: 1) the \textit{large-scale continual learning challenge} that assumes a practical demand to maintain long-term model effectiveness under dynamic item pools and distributional shifts; 2) the \textit{combinatorial diversity challenge} that requires the generation strategy to solve the accuracy-diversity trade-off in both the finer token level and the holistic item level; and 3) the \textit{multi-task reward balancing challenge}, which is particularly critical for modern generative models that can accurately model the sequence distribution but are less controllable for the multi-task demands. To address these challenges and further pave the way for the development of more realistic recommendation solutions, we introduce KuaiRecV2, a deliberately constructed benchmark with industrial-level datasets from Kuaishou. Specifically, we provide a large-scale interaction dataset with million-scale multi-modal item information and long-term interaction records across 30 days, with a dynamic video candidate pool. Additionally, we provide a rigorous benchmark that evaluates retrieval accuracy, diversity, and multi-task performance in one rubric system, where an effective advancement occurs if and only if the new method improves all metrics. The code is available at https://github.com/cxli2333/KuaiRecV2

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Learning for Nonlinear Nonholonomic Dynamics
papers.abstract: Learning the dynamics of mechanical systems subject to nonlinear nonholonomic constraints is challenging, as data-driven models may violate the underlying physical constraints, leading to inconsistent predictions. To address this problem, we develop a constraint-preserving learning framework based on the Lagrange-d'Alembert-Chetaev equations and tangency to the constraint submanifold, which together define an affine space of admissible accelerations. Using the kinetic-energy metric and the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, we construct a metric projector and the corresponding Chetaev correction. Embedding this geometric structure directly into a Gaussian process prior ensures that both prior and posterior dynamics satisfy the acceleration constraints exactly. We characterize the resulting reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), derive an adapted-coordinate representation, and establish nonexpansiveness and consistency transfer. Numerical experiments on a three-dimensional directional flocking system with up to 50 agents demonstrate exact constraint preservation and robustness to constraint-incompatible observations.

papers.title: Finite Bodies on Norton's Dome: Escape-Time Divergence and a Center-of-Mass Barrier Theorem
papers.abstract: Norton's dome illustrates how a Newtonian initial-value problem can admit both rest and delayed departure from the same initial state. We examine how this nonuniqueness changes when the point particle is replaced by a rigid sphere of positive radius. For a generalized family of Norton's domes, we show that any fixed positive sphere radius prevents spontaneous departure from rest at the apex. We then extend the analysis to more general bodies and establish two sufficient conditions: a geometric constraint on the distance between the center of mass and the apex, and an interior tangent ball condition for rigid bodies whose center of mass is vertically aligned with the initial contact point. Both arguments combine geometric estimates with an energy inequality and Grönwall's inequality. The first condition also applies to passive deformable bodies without releasable internal energy. These results identify explicit conditions under which finite-body geometry excludes the spontaneous motion allowed by Norton's point-particle model.

papers.title: Transverse impact of a Hertzian sphere with an infinite Rayleigh beam
papers.abstract: We study the impact of a Hertzian sphere on an infinite Rayleigh beam, which presents both interesting possibilities for numerical approximation as well as new insights in the multiple-contact-event regime. Here, Galerkin projection using an abstract continuous variable replaces the history-dependent convolution in the impact equations by a system of local-in-time ordinary differential equations. The corresponding approximate solutions are validated against direct numerical solution of the convolution-based formulation and show agreement. Unlike the corresponding Euler-Bernoulli beam impact problem, which is governed by a single nondimensional parameter, the Rayleigh beam impact dynamics is governed by two nondimensional parameters. A parametric study reveals three distinct impact regimes: one regime with a single contact followed by permanent separation, a second regime with a single contact that is sustained thereafter, and an intervening regime with initial separation followed by multiple contact events with diminishing amplitudes, leading eventually to sustained contact. Short- and long-time asymptotic analyses are used to characterize the boundaries between the permanent separation and the re-contact regimes in different parameter regimes. The three significant new aspects of this paper are the system itself (Rayleigh beam instead of Euler Bernoulli beam), the model order reduction achieved through Galerkin projection in an abstract domain, and the detailed parametric study leading to a simple qualitative picture of possible behaviours.

papers.title: Nevanlinna theory for generalized tropical meromorphic functions and applications to ultra-discrete equations
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to establish the tropical Nevanlinna theory to piecewise linear real functions with arbitrary first-kind discontinuities (called generalized tropical meromorphic functions). The key point is that we introduce the directional jump counting functions $J^+(r,f)$ and $J^-(r,f)$ for the case of arbitrary first-kind discontinuities to refine the single function $J(r,f)$ in the previous theory. We first obtain the new tropical version of the Poisson-Jensen formula, the first main theorem. Under the assumption that $f$ is slope-admissible, we show that $T(r,f)$ is nondecreasing and establish a logarithmic derivative lemma. These results unify the classical continuous case due to Halburd and Southall and the one-sided continuous case due to Halonen, Korhonen and Filipuk. As applications, we study several first-order and second-order ultra-discrete equations, showing that certain equations admit infinitely many generalized tropical meromorphic solutions, and that under suitable conditions infinite-order solutions also exist. Finally, using the logarithmic derivative lemma obtained above, we establish a tropical Clunie lemma.

papers.title: A Code-Level Audit of X
papers.abstract: The transparency regime of recommender systems on Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) is undergoing significant change under the EU Digital Services Act (DSA). The DSA requires platforms to disclose information about their recommendation pipelines and grants vetted researchers access to non-public data, which may extend to recommender code. However, it is not known to what extent such code releases enable substantive and meaningful third-party auditing of a production recommender system. We address this question by proposing a code-level audit methodology for recommender systems and applying it to the X platform, which has voluntarily open-sourced its recommender pipeline. Our methodology is a backwards-walk traversal of the repository, tracing each decision-relevant component from the user-facing timeline back to its upstream producers, checking that it is reachable from the served pipeline, and classifying each under a four-tier inspectability scheme. Applying this procedure, we identify 13 transparency dead-ends on the live serving path: models, services, label lists, and configuration values that the public code depends on but the release does not contain. We find that the components that decide which posts are filtered and how they are ranked fall into the two least inspectable tiers, a pattern that intensifies with the 2025 integration of the proprietary Grok language model into moderation, annotation, and ranking. We further show that the release keeps 2023 code that the 2025 pipeline no longer reaches, with 36 parameter references that would pass for dead-ends without a reachability check. Finally, we discuss which additional artifacts would be required for meaningful auditing.

papers.title: Agentic Orchestration for SLA-Constrained Network Slicing in Programmable Mobile Data Planes
papers.abstract: The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Technical Specification 23.501 (Release 17) defines Maximum Bit Rate (MBR) enforcement at the User Plane Function (UPF) in fifth-generation (5G) networks. Supporting differentiated service-level agreements across the radio access and core networks requires the UPF to enforce MBR limits according to configured slice priorities. During overload, the challenge is to adapt these limits while preserving that differentiation and avoiding oscillations. Building on programmable enforcement and intelligent orchestration, we propose an agentic control loop combining UPF telemetry with locally hosted Large Language Model (LLM) selection from a finite set of admissible rate candidates. Deterministic logic validates each selection and derives Packet Forwarding Control Protocol (PFCP) updates. The evaluated runs show no oscillations or fallbacks and unchanged highest-priority rate limits. These observations establish configuration preservation; delivered per-class QoS protection remains unmeasured.

papers.title: CODE-PIF: Convex/Deep (CODE) Multiview Pseudoinvariant Features for Multitemporal Multispectral Surface Reflectance Imagery
